ko.title: [농업 입문 #4] 당신의 토양은 은행 계좌입니다 — 입금과 출금이 작동하는 방식

segments.src: > Plants need 17 essential elements, but three of them (N, P, K) do most of the heavy lifting — and soil pH quietly decides how much of any of them a root can actually reach.
segments.tr: > 식물은 17가지 필수 원소가 필요하지만, 그중 3가지(N, P, K)가 핵심적인 역할을 담당합니다. 그리고 토양 pH는 이 원소들 중 뿌리가 실제로 흡수할 수 있는 양을 조용히 결정합니다.

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Think of soil as a checking account that plants draw from every day.
segments.tr: 토양을 식물이 매일 돈을 인출하는 당좌예금 계좌라고 생각해보세요.

segments.src: Plants build themselves out of **essential elements** — nutrients that, if missing, mean the plant literally cannot complete its life cycle.
segments.tr: 식물은 **필수 원소**로 자신을 구성합니다. 이는 부족할 경우 식물이 생명 주기를 문자 그대로 완료할 수 없는 영양소입니다.

segments.src: There are 17 of them.
segments.tr: 이러한 원소는 총 17가지가 있습니다.

segments.src: Three come free from air and water: carbon, hydrogen, oxygen.
segments.tr: 그중 3가지는 공기와 물에서 공짜로 얻어집니다: 탄소, 수소, 산소.

segments.src: The other 14 come from the soil.
segments.tr: 나머지 14가지는 토양에서 옵니다.

segments.src: Those 14 split into two groups by *quantity needed*, not importance:
segments.tr: 그 14가지 원소는 중요도가 아니라 *필요한 양*에 따라 두 그룹으로 나뉩니다:

segments.src: - **Macronutrients** (needed in large amounts): nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), plus calcium, magnesium, and sulfur.
segments.tr: - **다량영양소** (많은 양이 필요함): 질소(N), 인(P), 칼륨(K), 그리고 칼슘, 마그네슘, 황.

segments.src: - **Micronutrients** (needed in trace amounts): iron, manganese, zinc, copper, boron, molybdenum, chlorine, nickel.
segments.tr: - **미량영양소** (아주 적은 양이 필요함): 철, 망간, 아연, 구리, 붕소, 몰리브덴, 염소, 니켈.

segments.src: A micronutrient deficiency will kill a crop just as dead as a nitrogen shortage.
segments.tr: 미량영양소 결핍은 질소 부족만큼이나 확실하게 작물을 죽입니다.

segments.src: The difference is how much you have to add.
segments.tr: 차이점은 얼마나 많이 추가해야 하느냐에 있습니다.

segments.src: **The Big Three.** Every bag of fertilizer in the U.S.
segments.tr: **핵심 3원소.** 미국의 모든 비료 포대 앞면에는

segments.src: carries three numbers on the front — say, `10-10-10`.
segments.tr: 세 가지 숫자가 적혀 있습니다 — 예를 들어 `10-10-10`처럼 말이죠.

segments.src: That's the guaranteed analysis: percent nitrogen, percent phosphate (P₂O₅), percent potash (K₂O), by weight.
segments.tr: 이것은 보증 성분량으로, 중량 기준 질소 백분율, 인산(P₂O₅) 백분율, 가리(K₂O) 백분율을 뜻합니다.

segments.src: A 50 lb bag of 10-10-10 contains 5 lb of N, 5 lb of phosphate, and 5 lb of potash.
segments.tr: 10-10-10 비료 50파운드 포대에는 질소 5파운드, 인산 5파운드, 가리 5파운드가 들어 있습니다.

segments.src: The rest is carrier and filler.
segments.tr: 나머지는 운반체와 충전재입니다.

segments.src: Roughly what each does:
segments.tr: 각각이 하는 역할의 대략적인 내용:

segments.src: - **Nitrogen** — leaves and stems, chlorophyll, protein. Deficiency shows as pale yellowing on the *oldest* leaves first, because the plant scavenges N from old tissue and moves it to new growth.
segments.tr: - **질소** — 잎과 줄기, 엽록소, 단백질. 식물이 오래된 조직에서 질소를 회수하여 새로운 성장에 사용하기 때문에, 결핍 증상은 *가장 오래된* 잎에서 연한 황색화로 먼저 나타납니다.

segments.src: - **Phosphorus** — roots, energy transfer, flowering and seed set. Deficiency can show as dull purple-tinged leaves.
segments.tr: - **인** — 뿌리, 에너지 전달, 개화 및 종자 결실. 결핍 시 칙칙한 보랏빛이 도는 잎으로 나타날 수 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Potassium** — water regulation, stomatal control, disease resistance, stalk strength. Deficiency often shows as scorched leaf margins.
segments.tr: - **칼륨** — 수분 조절, 기공 조절, 내병성, 줄기 강도. 결핍은 종종 잎 가장자리가 타들어 가는 증상으로 나타납니다.

segments.src: **Now the part most people skip: pH.**
segments.tr: **이제 대부분의 사람이 건너뛰는 부분: pH.**

segments.src: Soil pH is a measure of how acidic or alkaline the soil solution is, on a 0–14 scale where 7 is neutral.
segments.tr: 토양 pH는 7을 중성으로 하는 0~14 눈금을 기준으로 토양 용액이 얼마나 산성인지 알칼리성인지 나타내는 척도입니다.

segments.src: It matters because **pH controls nutrient availability**.
segments.tr: 이것이 중요한 이유는 **pH가 영양소 가용성을 제어하기** 때문입니다.

segments.src: You can have plenty of phosphorus in the soil and still starve the crop, because at low pH the phosphorus binds with iron and aluminum into forms roots can't take up.
segments.tr: 토양에 인이 풍부해도 작물이 굶주릴 수 있는데, 낮은 pH에서는 인이 철 및 알루미늄과 결합하여 뿌리가 흡수할 수 없는 형태로 변하기 때문입니다.

segments.src: At high pH it binds with calcium instead.
segments.tr: 높은 pH에서는 대신 칼슘과 결합합니다.

segments.src: Phosphorus is most available roughly between pH 6.0 and 7.0 — which is why most field crops and garden vegetables are happiest in the pH 6.0–7.0 window.
segments.tr: 인은 대략 pH 6.0에서 7.0 사이일 때 가장 이용 가능성이 높습니다. 이것이 대부분의 밭작물과 정원 채소가 pH 6.0~7.0 범위에서 가장 잘 자라는 이유입니다.

segments.src: Iron, manganese, and zinc run the opposite way: they get *more* available as soil turns acidic.
segments.tr: 철, 망간, 아연은 정반대로 작동합니다. 토양이 산성으로 변할수록 이용 가능성이 *더 높아집니다*.

segments.src: That's why azaleas and blueberries — acid-lovers — go chlorotic and yellow in alkaline soil.
segments.tr: 이것이 진달래와 블루베리 같은 산성 토양을 좋아하는 식물이 알칼리성 토양에서 잎록소 결핍으로 노랗게 변하는 이유입니다.

segments.src: They can't get iron.
segments.tr: 철분을 흡수할 수 없기 때문입니다.

segments.src: **Buffering capacity** is why fixing pH is harder than it sounds.
segments.tr: **완충능력**은 pH를 교정하는 것이 생각보다 어려운 이유입니다.

segments.src: If you add acid to distilled water, the pH plunges.
segments.tr: 증류수에 산을 넣으면 pH가 급격히 떨어집니다.

segments.src: Add the same acid to soil and it barely moves.
segments.tr: 토양에 같은 산을 넣어도 pH는 거의 변하지 않습니다.

segments.src: That resistance is buffering, and it comes from the soil's reserve of exchangeable acidity sitting on clay particles and organic matter — a large hidden pool that keeps refilling the soil solution as you neutralize it.
segments.tr: 이러한 저항력이 바로 완충작용이며, 이는 점토 입자와 유기물에 부착된 교환성 산도 예비분에서 비롯됩니다. 이는 중화할 때마다 토양 용액을 계속해서 보충해 주는 커다란 숨겨진 풀입니다.

segments.src: Practical consequence: a heavy clay soil rich in organic matter needs *far more* lime to raise its pH one unit than a sandy soil does.
segments.tr: 실질적인 결과: 유기물이 풍부한 무거운 점토질 토양은 모래땅보다 pH를 1단위 높이는 데 *훨씬 더 많은* 석회가 필요합니다.

segments.src: That's why a soil test doesn't just report pH — it reports a **buffer pH** or **lime requirement**, which is the number that actually tells you how much lime to spread.
segments.tr: 이것이 토양 검사에서 단순히 pH만 보고하지 않고, 실제로 얼마만큼의 석회를 뿌려야 하는지 알려주는 **완충 pH**나 **석회 소요량**을 함께 보고하는 이유입니다.

segments.src: Soil test pH   -> where you are now
segments.tr: Soil test pH   -> where you are now

segments.src: Buffer pH      -> how hard it will be to move
segments.tr: Buffer pH      -> how hard it will be to move

segments.src: Lime rate      -> tons per acre to get where you want
segments.tr: Lime rate      -> tons per acre to get where you want

segments.src: The general rules of thumb: **lime** (calcium carbonate) raises pH; **elemental sulfur** lowers it.
segments.tr: 일반적인 경험 법칙: **석회**(탄산칼슘)는 pH를 높이고, **원소 황**은 낮춥니다.

segments.src: Both work slowly — months, sometimes a full season — because they depend on soil moisture, temperature, and microbial activity.
segments.tr: 두 가지 모두 토양 수분, 온도, 미생물 활동에 의존하기 때문에 몇 달, 때로는 한 시즌 전체에 걸쳐 서서히 작용합니다.

segments.src: One more piece of vocabulary that ties it together: **cation exchange capacity (CEC)**.
segments.tr: 이를 하나로 묶어주는 또 하나의 용어: **양이온 교환 용능(CEC)**.

segments.src: Clay and organic matter carry negative charges, and positively charged nutrients — calcium, magnesium, potassium, ammonium — stick to those sites like magnets on a fridge.
segments.tr: 점토와 유기물은 음전하를 띠고 있으며, 양전하를 띤 영양소(칼슘, 마그네슘, 칼륨, 암모늄)는 냉장고 자석처럼 이러한 부착 지점에 달라붙습니다.

segments.src: High CEC means a soil holds a large nutrient reserve and buffers strongly.
segments.tr: 높은 CEC는 토양이 다량의 영양소 예비분을 보유하고 강하게 완충함을 의미합니다.

segments.src: Low CEC (sandy soil) means nutrients leach through fast.
segments.tr: 낮은 CEC(모래땅)는 영양소가 빠르게 유실됨을 의미합니다.

segments.src: Same fertilizer, very different behavior.
segments.tr: 같은 비료라도 매우 다른 양상을 보입니다.

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: Say you're in Ohio and you plant tomatoes in the same backyard bed for the third summer running.
segments.tr: 오하이오주에 살면서 뒷마당 화단에 3년째 연속으로 토마토를 심는다고 가정해 보겠습니다.

segments.src: You fertilize religiously with a high-nitrogen lawn-style product because it's what's in the garage.
segments.tr: 차고에 있는 것이라는 이유로 고질소 잔디용 제품을 맹목적으로 시비합니다.

segments.src: You get magnificent, dark green, four-foot vines — and almost no fruit.
segments.tr: 그 결과 짙은 녹색을 띠는 4피트짜리 웅장한 덩굴은 얻지만, 열매는 거의 열리지 않습니다.

segments.src: That's textbook nutrient imbalance.
segments.tr: 이것이 교과서적인 영양 불균형입니다.

segments.src: Excess nitrogen pushes vegetative growth at the expense of flowering and fruit set.
segments.tr: 과도한 질소는 개화와 결실을 희생시키면서 영양 생장을 촉진합니다.

segments.src: Meanwhile, three seasons of removing tomatoes has been quietly withdrawing potassium and phosphorus from the account with no matching deposit.
segments.tr: 한편, 3시즌 동안 토마토를 수확해 가면서 상응하는 투입(입금) 없이 계좌에서 칼륨과 인을 조용히 인출해 갔습니다.

segments.src: And in much of the eastern U.S., where rainfall gradually leaches calcium and magnesium out of the topsoil, the pH has been drifting downward year over year — possibly into the mid-5s, where phosphorus availability drops sharply.
segments.tr: 또한 강우로 인해 표토에서 칼슘과 마그네슘이 점진적으로 용탈되는 미국 동부의 많은 지역에서는 pH가 해마다 낮아져 어쩌면 5.5 중간 수준까지 떨어졌을 수 있으며, 이 경우 인의 가용성이 급격히 떨어집니다.

segments.src: The fix costs less than a bag of fertilizer.
segments.tr: 해결 비용은 비료 한 포대 값보다 적게 듭니다.

segments.src: Nearly every state has a land-grant university extension service — Ohio State, Penn State, NC State, Texas A&M — running soil testing labs, typically in the $15–$25 range per sample.
segments.tr: 거의 모든 주에는 오하이오 주립대, 펜실베이니아 주립대, 노스캐롤라이나 주립대, 텍사스 A&M 등 토양 검사소를 운영하는 랜드그랜트 대학 확장 서비스가 있으며, 샘플당 보통 15~25달러 범위입니다.

segments.src: You send in a composite of 10–15 cores from around the bed.
segments.tr: 화단 곳곳에서 채취한 10~15개의 코어 샘플을 섞어서 보냅니다.

segments.src: What comes back is pH, buffer pH, extractable P and K, calcium, magnesium, organic matter percentage, and CEC, plus a recommendation in pounds per 1,000 square feet.
segments.tr: 결과로 나오는 것은 pH, 완충 pH, 추출 가능한 P와 K, 칼슘, 마그네슘, 유기물 함량 백분율, CEC이며, 1,000제곱피트당 파운드 단위의 시비 추천량도 함께 제공됩니다.

segments.src: If the report says pH 5.4 with a lime requirement of 50 lb per 1,000 sq ft, spreading that lime the previous fall will do more for next year's tomatoes than any amount of fertilizer applied in June.
segments.tr: 보고서에 1,000제곱피트당 50파운드의 석회 소요량과 함께 pH 5.4라고 적혀 있다면, 전년도 가을에 그 석회를 뿌려주는 것이 6월에 어떤 비료를 주는 것보다 내년 토마토에 더 큰 도움이 됩니다.

segments.src: You're not adding nutrients — you're unlocking the ones already sitting there.
segments.tr: 영양소를 새로 추가하는 것이 아니라 이미 그곳에 있는 영양소를 활성화하는 것입니다.

segments.src: There's an environmental side too.
segments.tr: 환경적인 측면도 있습니다.

segments.src: Nutrients you apply beyond what the crop can use don't vanish.
segments.tr: 작물이 이용할 수 있는 양을 초과하여 시비한 영양소는 사라지지 않습니다.

segments.src: Nitrate leaches into groundwater; phosphorus runs off into surface water and feeds algal blooms.
segments.tr: 질산염은 지하수로 스며들고, 인은 지표수로 유입되어 녹조 현상을 유발합니다.

segments.src: The recurring summer blooms in Lake Erie and the hypoxic "dead zone" in the Gulf of Mexico are both driven substantially by nutrient runoff from a very large watershed.
segments.tr: 이리호의 반복되는 여름철 녹조와 멕시코만의 저산소 "죽음의 바다"는 모두 매우 넓은 유역에서 흘러드는 영양 염류 유출에 크게 기인합니다.

segments.src: Matching the rate to the actual soil test is the single cheapest thing that helps both your yield and the water downstream.
segments.tr: 실제 토양 검사 결과에 시비량을 맞추는 것이 수확량과 하류의 수질 모두에 도움이 되는 가장 저렴한 단 하나의 방법입니다.

segments.src: The professional framing for this is the **4Rs**: Right source, Right rate, Right time, Right place.
segments.tr: 이를 전문적으로 표현한 것이 **4R**: 올바른 시비원(Right source), 올바른 시비량(Right rate), 올바른 시기(Right time), 올바른 시비 위치(Right place)입니다.

segments.src: Pick the fertilizer form that fits, apply only what the test calls for, put it down when the crop can use it, and place it where roots will find it.
segments.tr: 상황에 맞는 비료 형태를 선택하고, 검사에서 요구하는 양만 시비하며, 작물이 필요로 할 때 주고, 뿌리가 찾을 수 있는 위치에 시비하세요.

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## 3줄 정리

segments.src: 1. Plants need 17 essential elements; N, P, and K are needed in the largest amounts, which is why every fertilizer bag carries three numbers (`N-P₂O₅-K₂O`) on the front.
segments.tr: 1. 식물에는 17가지 필수 원소가 필요하며, N, P, K가 가장 많은 양으로 필요하기 때문에 모든 비료 포대 앞면에는 세 가지 숫자(`N-P₂O₅-K₂O`)가 적혀 있습니다.

segments.src: 2. Soil pH governs whether nutrients are chemically *available* to roots — phosphorus peaks around pH 6.0–7.0, while iron and zinc become more available as soil turns acidic.
segments.tr: 2. 토양 pH는 영양소가 뿌리에 화학적으로 *이용 가능한지*를 좌우합니다. 인은 pH 6.0~7.0 부근에서 최고조에 달하고, 철과 아연은 토양이 산성화될수록 이용 가능성이 높아집니다.

segments.src: 3. Buffering capacity, driven by clay and organic matter, resists pH change — so a soil test's buffer pH, not the pH alone, tells you how much lime to apply.
segments.tr: 3. 점토와 유기물에 의해 주도되는 완충능력은 pH 변화에 저항하므로, pH 단독이 아니라 토양 검사의 완충 pH가 시비해야 할 석회 양을 알려줍니다.

segments.src: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈
segments.tr: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈

segments.src: **Q1.** A 50 lb bag of fertilizer is labeled `10-20-10`.
segments.tr: **Q1.** 비료 50파운드 포대에 `10-20-10`이라고 적혀 있습니다.

segments.src: How many pounds of actual phosphate (P₂O₅) does it contain?
segments.tr: 실제 인산(P₂O₅)은 몇 파운드 포함되어 있나요?

segments.tr: - A) 5 lb

segments.src: **Q2.** O/X — Two soils both test at pH 5.5, so they will both need the same amount of lime to reach pH 6.5.
segments.tr: **Q2.** O/X — 두 토양 모두 pH 5.5로 측정되었으므로, pH 6.5에 도달하려면 두 토양 모두 동일한 양의 석회가 필요합니다.

segments.src: **Q3.** A gardener's soil has plenty of iron in it, but the plants show yellowing between the leaf veins (chlorosis).
segments.tr: **Q3.** 한 정원사의 토양에 철분이 풍부하지만, 식물의 잎맥 사이에 황화 현상(클로로시스)이 나타납니다.

segments.src: Which condition is the most likely cause?
segments.tr: 가장 가능성이 높은 원인은 어떤 조건인가요?

segments.src: - A) Soil pH is too low (strongly acidic)
segments.tr: - A) 토양 pH가 너무 낮음(강산성)

segments.src: - B) Soil pH is too high (alkaline)
segments.tr: - B) 토양 pH가 너무 높음(알칼리성)

segments.src: - C) Nitrogen was over-applied
segments.tr: - C) 질소가 과다 시비됨

segments.src: - D) The soil has no cation exchange capacity
segments.tr: - D) 토양에 양이온 교환 능력이 없음

segments.src: ## 📚 오늘의 용어
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Essential element** — A nutrient a plant cannot complete its life cycle without, and whose role no other element can substitute for; there are 17.
segments.tr: - **필수 원소(Essential element)** — 식물이 생명 주기를 완료하는 데 없어서는 안 되며, 다른 어떤 원소도 그 역할을 대신할 수 없는 영양소로 총 17가지가 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Macronutrient / Micronutrient** — Classification by the *amount* a plant needs, not by importance; both categories are equally essential.
segments.tr: - **다량영양소 / 미량영양소** — 중요도가 아니라 식물이 필요로 하는 *양*에 따른 분류이며, 두 범주 모두 똑같이 필수적입니다.

segments.src: - **Guaranteed analysis (N-P-K)** — The three numbers on a fertilizer label giving percent nitrogen, percent phosphate (P₂O₅), and percent potash (K₂O) by weight.
segments.tr: - **보증 성분량(N-P-K)** — 중량 기준 질소 백분율, 인산(P₂O₅) 백분율, 가리(K₂O) 백분율을 나타내는 비료 라벨의 세 가지 숫자입니다.

segments.src: - **Soil pH** — The acidity or alkalinity of the soil solution on a 0–14 scale; it determines the chemical form, and therefore the availability, of most nutrients.
segments.tr: - **토양 pH** — 0~14 눈금으로 나타낸 토양 용액의 산성도 또는 알칼리도로, 대부분의 영양소의 화학적 형태와 그에 따른 가용성을 결정합니다.

segments.src: - **Buffering capacity** — A soil's resistance to pH change, supplied by exchangeable acidity held on clay and organic matter; it sets how much lime or sulfur is actually required.
segments.tr: - **완충능력** — 점토와 유기물에 보유된 교환성 산도에 의해 제공되는 pH 변화에 대한 토양의 저항력으로, 석회나 황이 실제로 얼마나 필요한지 결정합니다.

segments.src: - **Cation exchange capacity (CEC)** — The soil's total capacity to hold positively charged nutrients on negatively charged clay and organic matter surfaces; a proxy for nutrient-holding ability.
segments.tr: - **양이온 교환 용능(CEC)** — 음전하를 띤 점토 및 유기물 표면에 양전하를 띤 영양소를 보유하는 토양의 총 능력으로, 영양소 보유 능력을 나타내는 지표입니다.

segments.src: *정답: **Q1 → B (10 lb).** The middle number is percent by weight, so 20% of 50 lb = 10 lb of phosphate.
segments.tr: *정답: **Q1 → B (10 lb).** 가운데 숫자는 중량 기준 백분율이므로 50 lb의 20% = 인산 10 lb입니다.

segments.src: Note this is P₂O₅, the oxide form used on labels, not elemental phosphorus — elemental P would be about 44% of that figure.*
segments.tr: 이는 원소 형태의 인이 아니라 라벨에 사용되는 산화물 형태인 P₂O₅이며, 원소 P는 이 수치의 약 44%에 해당한다는 점에 유의하세요.*

segments.src: ***Q2 → X (False).** Identical pH does not mean identical lime requirement.
segments.tr: ***Q2 → X (거짓).** pH가 같다고 해서 석회 소요량이 같다는 뜻은 아닙니다.

segments.src: A heavy clay soil high in organic matter has a large reserve of exchangeable acidity — high buffering — and may need several times the lime a sandy soil needs to make the same pH move.
segments.tr: 유기물이 풍부한 무거운 점토질 토양은 교환성 산도 예비분이 많아 완충능력이 크므로, 모래땅과 같은 pH 변화를 만드는 데 모래땅보다 몇 배 더 많은 석회가 필요할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: This is exactly why soil test reports include a buffer pH.*
segments.tr: 이것이 바로 토양 검사 보고서에 완충 pH가 포함되는 이유입니다.*

segments.src: ***Q3 → B.** Iron becomes progressively less soluble as pH rises; in alkaline soil it precipitates into forms roots cannot absorb.
segments.tr: ***Q3 → B.** 철은 pH가 상승할수록 용해도가 점차 떨어집니다. 알칼리성 토양에서는 뿌리가 흡수할 수 없는 형태로 침전됩니다.

segments.src: The plant is iron-deficient despite iron being physically present — a good illustration that total nutrient content and plant-available nutrient content are two different things.
segments.tr: 철분이 물리적으로 존재함에도 불구하고 식물에 철 결핍이 발생하는 것입니다. 이는 총 영양소 함량과 식물이 이용 가능한 영양소 함량이 서로 다르다는 것을 보여주는 좋은 예입니다.

segments.src: Interveinal chlorosis on the youngest leaves is the classic symptom, because iron is not readily remobilized within the plant.*
segments.tr: 철분은 식물 내에서 쉽게 재이동되지 않기 때문에 가장 어린 잎에 나타나는 엽맥 간 황화 현상이 전형적인 증상입니다.*

zh.title: [农业基础 #4] 你的土壤就像银行账户——存款和取款的运作方式如下

segments.src: > Plants need 17 essential elements, but three of them (N, P, K) do most of the heavy lifting — and soil pH quietly decides how much of any of them a root can actually reach.
segments.tr: > 植物需要 17 种必需元素，但其中三种（氮、磷、钾）承担了大部分繁重的工作——而土壤 pH 值则默默决定了根系实际上能接触到多少这些元素。

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Think of soil as a checking account that plants draw from every day.
segments.tr: 把土壤想象成一个植物每天都在从中取款的支票账户。

segments.src: Plants build themselves out of **essential elements** — nutrients that, if missing, mean the plant literally cannot complete its life cycle.
segments.tr: 植物利用**必需元素**来构建自身——如果缺少这些营养物质，植物就无法完成其生命周期。

segments.src: There are 17 of them.
segments.tr: 共有 17 种必需元素。

segments.src: Three come free from air and water: carbon, hydrogen, oxygen.
segments.tr: 其中三种来自空气和水：碳、氢、氧。

segments.src: The other 14 come from the soil.
segments.tr: 其余 14 种来自土壤。

segments.src: Those 14 split into two groups by *quantity needed*, not importance:
segments.tr: 这 14 种元素根据*所需数量*（而非重要性）分为两组：

segments.src: - **Macronutrients** (needed in large amounts): nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), plus calcium, magnesium, and sulfur.
segments.tr: - **大量营养元素**（需要量大）：氮 (N)、磷 (P)、钾 (K)，以及钙、镁和硫。

segments.src: - **Micronutrients** (needed in trace amounts): iron, manganese, zinc, copper, boron, molybdenum, chlorine, nickel.
segments.tr: - **微量营养元素**（需要量极少）：铁、锰、锌、铜、硼、钼、氯、镍。

segments.src: A micronutrient deficiency will kill a crop just as dead as a nitrogen shortage.
segments.tr: 微量营养元素缺乏会导致作物死亡，其后果与氮缺乏一样严重。

segments.src: The difference is how much you have to add.
segments.tr: 区别在于你需要添加的量不同。

segments.src: **The Big Three.** Every bag of fertilizer in the U.S.
segments.tr: **三大元素。** 美国每一袋肥料的正面

segments.src: carries three numbers on the front — say, `10-10-10`.
segments.tr: 都印有三个数字——例如 `10-10-10`。

segments.src: That's the guaranteed analysis: percent nitrogen, percent phosphate (P₂O₅), percent potash (K₂O), by weight.
segments.tr: 这是保证分析值：按重量计算的氮百分比、磷酸盐 (P₂O₅) 百分比、钾肥 (K₂O) 百分比。

segments.src: A 50 lb bag of 10-10-10 contains 5 lb of N, 5 lb of phosphate, and 5 lb of potash.
segments.tr: 一袋 50 磅重的 10-10-10 肥料含有 5 磅氮、5 磅磷酸盐和 5 磅钾肥。

segments.src: The rest is carrier and filler.
segments.tr: 其余部分是载体和填充剂。

segments.src: Roughly what each does:
segments.tr: 它们各自的大致作用：

segments.src: - **Nitrogen** — leaves and stems, chlorophyll, protein. Deficiency shows as pale yellowing on the *oldest* leaves first, because the plant scavenges N from old tissue and moves it to new growth.
segments.tr: - **氮** — 叶片和茎秆、叶绿素、蛋白质。缺乏时，*最老*的叶片首先出现苍白黄化，因为植物会从旧组织中回收氮并将其输送到新生长部位。

segments.src: - **Phosphorus** — roots, energy transfer, flowering and seed set. Deficiency can show as dull purple-tinged leaves.
segments.tr: - **磷** — 根系、能量转移、开花和结实。缺乏时可能表现为叶片呈暗紫色。

segments.src: - **Potassium** — water regulation, stomatal control, disease resistance, stalk strength. Deficiency often shows as scorched leaf margins.
segments.tr: - **钾** — 水分调节、气孔控制、抗病性、茎秆强度。缺乏时通常表现为叶缘焦枯。

segments.src: **Now the part most people skip: pH.**
segments.tr: **现在是大多数人忽略的部分：pH 值。**

segments.src: Soil pH is a measure of how acidic or alkaline the soil solution is, on a 0–14 scale where 7 is neutral.
segments.tr: 土壤 pH 值是衡量土壤溶液酸碱度的指标，范围为 0–14，其中 7 为中性。

segments.src: It matters because **pH controls nutrient availability**.
segments.tr: 它之所以重要，是因为 **pH 值控制着养分的有效性**。

segments.src: You can have plenty of phosphorus in the soil and still starve the crop, because at low pH the phosphorus binds with iron and aluminum into forms roots can't take up.
segments.tr: 即使土壤中有充足的磷，作物仍可能挨饿，因为在低 pH 值下，磷会与铁和铝结合成根系无法吸收的形式。

segments.src: At high pH it binds with calcium instead.
segments.tr: 在高 pH 值下，它则会与钙结合。

segments.src: Phosphorus is most available roughly between pH 6.0 and 7.0 — which is why most field crops and garden vegetables are happiest in the pH 6.0–7.0 window.
segments.tr: 磷在大约 pH 6.0 到 7.0 之间最有效——这就是为什么大多数大田作物和园艺蔬菜在 pH 6.0–7.0 的范围内生长得最好。

segments.src: Iron, manganese, and zinc run the opposite way: they get *more* available as soil turns acidic.
segments.tr: 铁、锰和锌的情况恰恰相反：随着土壤变酸，它们的有效性会*增加*。

segments.src: That's why azaleas and blueberries — acid-lovers — go chlorotic and yellow in alkaline soil.
segments.tr: 这就是为什么杜鹃花和蓝莓（喜酸植物）在碱性土壤中会失绿发黄。

segments.src: They can't get iron.
segments.tr: 因为它们无法获取铁元素。

segments.src: **Buffering capacity** is why fixing pH is harder than it sounds.
segments.tr: **缓冲能力**是调节 pH 值比听起来更难的原因。

segments.src: If you add acid to distilled water, the pH plunges.
segments.tr: 如果你在蒸馏水中加入酸，pH 值会骤降。

segments.src: Add the same acid to soil and it barely moves.
segments.tr: 而在土壤中加入同样的酸，pH 值几乎不会变动。

segments.src: That resistance is buffering, and it comes from the soil's reserve of exchangeable acidity sitting on clay particles and organic matter — a large hidden pool that keeps refilling the soil solution as you neutralize it.
segments.tr: 这种抵抗力就是缓冲作用，它来自土壤中储存在粘土颗粒和有机质上的可交换酸度——这是一个巨大的隐藏库，当你中和土壤溶液时，它会不断补充。

segments.src: Practical consequence: a heavy clay soil rich in organic matter needs *far more* lime to raise its pH one unit than a sandy soil does.
segments.tr: 实际后果：富含有机质的重粘土土壤，要将其 pH 值提高一个单位，所需的石灰量要*远多于*沙质土壤。

segments.src: That's why a soil test doesn't just report pH — it reports a **buffer pH** or **lime requirement**, which is the number that actually tells you how much lime to spread.
segments.tr: 这就是为什么土壤测试不仅报告 pH 值，还会报告 **缓冲 pH 值** 或 **石灰需求量**，这才是真正告诉你需要撒多少石灰的数字。

segments.src: Soil test pH   -> where you are now
segments.tr: Soil test pH   -> where you are now

segments.src: Buffer pH      -> how hard it will be to move
segments.tr: Buffer pH      -> how hard it will be to move

segments.src: Lime rate      -> tons per acre to get where you want
segments.tr: Lime rate      -> tons per acre to get where you want

segments.src: The general rules of thumb: **lime** (calcium carbonate) raises pH; **elemental sulfur** lowers it.
segments.tr: 一般的经验法则：**石灰**（碳酸钙）提高 pH 值；**元素硫**降低 pH 值。

segments.src: Both work slowly — months, sometimes a full season — because they depend on soil moisture, temperature, and microbial activity.
segments.tr: 两者起效都很慢——需要几个月，有时甚至一个完整的季节——因为它们依赖于土壤湿度、温度和微生物活动。

segments.src: One more piece of vocabulary that ties it together: **cation exchange capacity (CEC)**.
segments.tr: 另一个将这一切联系起来的词汇是：**阳离子交换量 (CEC)**。

segments.src: Clay and organic matter carry negative charges, and positively charged nutrients — calcium, magnesium, potassium, ammonium — stick to those sites like magnets on a fridge.
segments.tr: 粘土和有机质带有负电荷，而带正电的营养物质——钙、镁、钾、铵——就像冰箱上的磁铁一样吸附在这些位点上。

segments.src: High CEC means a soil holds a large nutrient reserve and buffers strongly.
segments.tr: 高 CEC 意味着土壤拥有大量的养分储备，并且缓冲能力强。

segments.src: Low CEC (sandy soil) means nutrients leach through fast.
segments.tr: 低 CEC（沙质土壤）意味着养分流失很快。

segments.src: Same fertilizer, very different behavior.
segments.tr: 同样的肥料，表现却截然不同。

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: Say you're in Ohio and you plant tomatoes in the same backyard bed for the third summer running.
segments.tr: 假设你在俄亥俄州，连续第三个夏天在同一个后院花坛里种植西红柿。

segments.src: You fertilize religiously with a high-nitrogen lawn-style product because it's what's in the garage.
segments.tr: 你虔诚地使用车库里现成的高氮草坪肥料。

segments.src: You get magnificent, dark green, four-foot vines — and almost no fruit.
segments.tr: 你得到了茂盛、深绿、四英尺高的藤蔓——但几乎没有果实。

segments.src: That's textbook nutrient imbalance.
segments.tr: 这就是教科书式的养分失衡。

segments.src: Excess nitrogen pushes vegetative growth at the expense of flowering and fruit set.
segments.tr: 过量的氮促进了营养生长，却牺牲了开花和结果。

segments.src: Meanwhile, three seasons of removing tomatoes has been quietly withdrawing potassium and phosphorus from the account with no matching deposit.
segments.tr: 与此同时，三个季节的西红柿采收一直在默默地从账户中提取钾和磷，却没有相应的存款。

segments.src: And in much of the eastern U.S., where rainfall gradually leaches calcium and magnesium out of the topsoil, the pH has been drifting downward year over year — possibly into the mid-5s, where phosphorus availability drops sharply.
segments.tr: 在美国东部大部分地区，降雨会逐渐将表土中的钙和镁淋失，pH 值逐年下降——可能降至 5.5 左右，此时磷的有效性会急剧下降。

segments.src: The fix costs less than a bag of fertilizer.
segments.tr: 解决办法的成本比一袋肥料还低。

segments.src: Nearly every state has a land-grant university extension service — Ohio State, Penn State, NC State, Texas A&M — running soil testing labs, typically in the $15–$25 range per sample.
segments.tr: 几乎每个州都有赠地大学推广服务机构——如俄亥俄州立大学、宾夕法尼亚州立大学、北卡罗来纳州立大学、德克萨斯农工大学——运营着土壤测试实验室，每个样本的费用通常在 15 到 25 美元之间。

segments.src: You send in a composite of 10–15 cores from around the bed.
segments.tr: 你只需从花坛周围采集 10–15 个土芯样本混合送检。

segments.src: What comes back is pH, buffer pH, extractable P and K, calcium, magnesium, organic matter percentage, and CEC, plus a recommendation in pounds per 1,000 square feet.
segments.tr: 返回的报告会包含 pH 值、缓冲 pH 值、可提取磷和钾、钙、镁、有机质百分比和 CEC，以及每 1,000 平方英尺所需的磅数建议。

segments.src: If the report says pH 5.4 with a lime requirement of 50 lb per 1,000 sq ft, spreading that lime the previous fall will do more for next year's tomatoes than any amount of fertilizer applied in June.
segments.tr: 如果报告显示 pH 5.4，石灰需求量为每 1,000 平方英尺 50 磅，那么在前一年秋天撒上这些石灰，对明年西红柿的帮助远胜于六月份施用的任何数量的肥料。

segments.src: You're not adding nutrients — you're unlocking the ones already sitting there.
segments.tr: 你不是在添加养分——你是在解锁那些已经存在于土壤中的养分。

segments.src: There's an environmental side too.
segments.tr: 这还有环境方面的影响。

segments.src: Nutrients you apply beyond what the crop can use don't vanish.
segments.tr: 你施用的超出作物需求量的养分并不会消失。

segments.src: Nitrate leaches into groundwater; phosphorus runs off into surface water and feeds algal blooms.
segments.tr: 硝酸盐会淋溶到地下水中；磷会径流到地表水中并滋生藻类爆发。

segments.src: The recurring summer blooms in Lake Erie and the hypoxic "dead zone" in the Gulf of Mexico are both driven substantially by nutrient runoff from a very large watershed.
segments.tr: 伊利湖反复出现的夏季藻华和墨西哥湾的缺氧“死区”，很大程度上都是由大流域的养分径流驱动的。

segments.src: Matching the rate to the actual soil test is the single cheapest thing that helps both your yield and the water downstream.
segments.tr: 根据实际土壤测试结果来匹配施肥量，是既能帮助你的产量又能保护下游水质的最廉价方法。

segments.src: The professional framing for this is the **4Rs**: Right source, Right rate, Right time, Right place.
segments.tr: 对此的专业表述是 **4R 原则**：正确的来源 (Right source)、正确的用量 (Right rate)、正确的时间 (Right time)、正确的地点 (Right place)。

segments.src: Pick the fertilizer form that fits, apply only what the test calls for, put it down when the crop can use it, and place it where roots will find it.
segments.tr: 选择合适的肥料形式，只施用测试要求的量，在作物能利用时施用，并将其放置在根系能找到的地方。

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## 3줄 정리

segments.src: 1. Plants need 17 essential elements; N, P, and K are needed in the largest amounts, which is why every fertilizer bag carries three numbers (`N-P₂O₅-K₂O`) on the front.
segments.tr: 1. 植物需要 17 种必需元素；氮、磷、钾的需求量最大，这就是为什么每袋肥料正面都印有三个数字 (`N-P₂O₅-K₂O`) 的原因。

segments.src: 2. Soil pH governs whether nutrients are chemically *available* to roots — phosphorus peaks around pH 6.0–7.0, while iron and zinc become more available as soil turns acidic.
segments.tr: 2. 土壤 pH 值决定了养分在化学上是否对根系*有效*——磷在 pH 6.0–7.0 左右达到峰值，而铁和锌随着土壤变酸变得更有效。

segments.src: 3. Buffering capacity, driven by clay and organic matter, resists pH change — so a soil test's buffer pH, not the pH alone, tells you how much lime to apply.
segments.tr: 3. 由粘土和有机质驱动的缓冲能力会抵抗 pH 值的变化——因此，土壤测试中的缓冲 pH 值（而非单纯的 pH 值）才能告诉你需要施用多少石灰。

segments.src: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈
segments.tr: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈

segments.src: **Q1.** A 50 lb bag of fertilizer is labeled `10-20-10`.
How many pounds of actual phosphate (P₂O₅) does it contain?
segments.tr: 它含有多少磅实际的磷酸盐 (P₂O₅)？

segments.src: - A) 5 lb
segments.tr: - A) 5 磅

segments.src: - B) 10 lb
- C) 20 lb
- D) 50 lb
**Q2.** O/X — Two soils both test at pH 5.5, so they will both need the same amount of lime to reach pH 6.5.
segments.tr: **Q2.** 判断对错 — 两块土壤的 pH 值测试均为 5.5，因此它们都需要相同数量的石灰才能达到 pH 6.5。

segments.src: **Q3.** A gardener's soil has plenty of iron in it, but the plants show yellowing between the leaf veins (chlorosis).
segments.tr: **Q3.** 一位园丁的土壤中有充足的铁，但植物叶脉间出现黄化（失绿症）。

segments.src: Which condition is the most likely cause?
segments.tr: 哪种情况是最可能的原因？

segments.src: - A) Soil pH is too low (strongly acidic)
segments.tr: - A) 土壤 pH 值过低（强酸性）

segments.src: - B) Soil pH is too high (alkaline)
segments.tr: - B) 土壤 pH 值过高（碱性）

segments.src: - C) Nitrogen was over-applied
segments.tr: - C) 氮肥施用过量

segments.src: - D) The soil has no cation exchange capacity
segments.tr: - D) 土壤没有阳离子交换能力

segments.src: ## 📚 오늘의 용어
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Essential element** — A nutrient a plant cannot complete its life cycle without, and whose role no other element can substitute for; there are 17.
segments.tr: - **必需元素** — 植物没有它就无法完成生命周期，且其作用无法被其他元素替代的营养物质；共有 17 种。

segments.src: - **Macronutrient / Micronutrient** — Classification by the *amount* a plant needs, not by importance; both categories are equally essential.
segments.tr: - **大量营养元素 / 微量营养元素** — 根据植物所需的*数量*而非重要性进行的分类；两类营养元素同样重要。

segments.src: - **Guaranteed analysis (N-P-K)** — The three numbers on a fertilizer label giving percent nitrogen, percent phosphate (P₂O₅), and percent potash (K₂O) by weight.
segments.tr: - **保证分析值 (N-P-K)** — 肥料标签上的三个数字，按重量给出氮百分比、磷酸盐 (P₂O₅) 百分比和钾肥 (K₂O) 百分比。

segments.src: - **Soil pH** — The acidity or alkalinity of the soil solution on a 0–14 scale; it determines the chemical form, and therefore the availability, of most nutrients.
segments.tr: - **土壤 pH 值** — 土壤溶液在 0–14 标度上的酸碱度；它决定了大多数养分的化学形式，进而决定了其有效性。

segments.src: - **Buffering capacity** — A soil's resistance to pH change, supplied by exchangeable acidity held on clay and organic matter; it sets how much lime or sulfur is actually required.
segments.tr: - **缓冲能力** — 土壤对 pH 值变化的抵抗力，由粘土和有机质上持有的可交换酸度提供；它决定了实际需要多少石灰或硫。

segments.src: - **Cation exchange capacity (CEC)** — The soil's total capacity to hold positively charged nutrients on negatively charged clay and organic matter surfaces; a proxy for nutrient-holding ability.
segments.tr: - **阳离子交换量 (CEC)** — 土壤在带负电的粘土和有机质表面保持带正电养分的总能力；是养分保持能力的指标。

segments.src: *정답: **Q1 → B (10 lb).** The middle number is percent by weight, so 20% of 50 lb = 10 lb of phosphate.
segments.tr: *答案: **Q1 → B (10 磅)。** 中间的数字是重量百分比，所以 50 磅的 20% = 10 磅磷酸盐。

segments.src: Note this is P₂O₅, the oxide form used on labels, not elemental phosphorus — elemental P would be about 44% of that figure.*
segments.tr: 注意这是 P₂O₅，即标签上使用的氧化物形式，而不是元素磷——元素磷大约占该数字的 44%。*

segments.src: ***Q2 → X (False).** Identical pH does not mean identical lime requirement.
segments.tr: ***Q2 → X (错误)。** 相同的 pH 值并不意味着相同的石灰需求量。

segments.src: A heavy clay soil high in organic matter has a large reserve of exchangeable acidity — high buffering — and may need several times the lime a sandy soil needs to make the same pH move.
segments.tr: 富含有机质的重粘土土壤拥有大量的可交换酸度储备——缓冲能力高——要达到同样的 pH 值变化，可能需要比沙质土壤多几倍的石灰。

segments.src: This is exactly why soil test reports include a buffer pH.*
segments.tr: 这正是土壤测试报告包含缓冲 pH 值的原因。*

segments.src: ***Q3 → B.** Iron becomes progressively less soluble as pH rises; in alkaline soil it precipitates into forms roots cannot absorb.
segments.tr: ***Q3 → B。** 随着 pH 值升高，铁的溶解度逐渐降低；在碱性土壤中，它会沉淀成根系无法吸收的形式。

segments.src: The plant is iron-deficient despite iron being physically present — a good illustration that total nutrient content and plant-available nutrient content are two different things.
segments.tr: 尽管土壤中实际存在铁，但植物仍表现出缺铁症状——这很好地说明了总养分含量和植物可利用养分含量是两码事。

segments.src: Interveinal chlorosis on the youngest leaves is the classic symptom, because iron is not readily remobilized within the plant.*
segments.tr: 幼叶上的叶脉间失绿是典型的症状，因为铁在植物体内不易重新移动。*

hi.title: [Agriculture 101 #4] आपकी मिट्टी एक बैंक खाते की तरह है — जानें कि जमा और निकासी कैसे काम करती है

segments.src: > Plants need 17 essential elements, but three of them (N, P, K) do most of the heavy lifting — and soil pH quietly decides how much of any of them a root can actually reach.
segments.tr: > पौधों को 17 आवश्यक तत्वों की आवश्यकता होती है, लेकिन उनमें से तीन (N, P, K) सबसे अधिक काम करते हैं — और मिट्टी का pH चुपचाप यह तय करता है कि उनमें से कोई भी तत्व जड़ तक वास्तव में कितना पहुँच सकता है।

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Think of soil as a checking account that plants draw from every day.
segments.tr: मिट्टी को एक चालू खाते (checking account) के रूप में सोचें जिससे पौधे हर दिन निकासी करते हैं।

segments.src: Plants build themselves out of **essential elements** — nutrients that, if missing, mean the plant literally cannot complete its life cycle.
segments.tr: पौधे खुद को **आवश्यक तत्वों (essential elements)** से बनाते हैं — वे पोषक तत्व जिनके बिना पौधा अपना जीवन चक्र पूरा नहीं कर सकता।

segments.src: There are 17 of them.
segments.tr: ऐसे 17 तत्व हैं।

segments.src: Three come free from air and water: carbon, hydrogen, oxygen.
segments.tr: तीन हवा और पानी से मुफ्त में मिलते हैं: कार्बन, हाइड्रोजन, ऑक्सीजन।

segments.src: The other 14 come from the soil.
segments.tr: बाकी 14 मिट्टी से आते हैं।

segments.src: Those 14 split into two groups by *quantity needed*, not importance:
segments.tr: वे 14 तत्व *आवश्यकता की मात्रा* के आधार पर दो समूहों में विभाजित हैं, न कि महत्व के आधार पर:

segments.src: - **Macronutrients** (needed in large amounts): nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), plus calcium, magnesium, and sulfur.
segments.tr: - **मैक्रोन्यूट्रिएंट्स (Macronutrients)** (बड़ी मात्रा में आवश्यक): नाइट्रोजन (N), फास्फोरस (P), पोटेशियम (K), साथ ही कैल्शियम, मैग्नीशियम और सल्फर।

segments.src: - **Micronutrients** (needed in trace amounts): iron, manganese, zinc, copper, boron, molybdenum, chlorine, nickel.
segments.tr: - **माइक्रोन्यूट्रिएंट्स (Micronutrients)** (अल्प मात्रा में आवश्यक): लोहा, मैंगनीज, जस्ता, तांबा, बोरॉन, मोलिब्डेनम, क्लोरीन, निकल।

segments.src: A micronutrient deficiency will kill a crop just as dead as a nitrogen shortage.
segments.tr: माइक्रोन्यूट्रिएंट की कमी फसल को उतनी ही बुरी तरह मार देगी जितनी नाइट्रोजन की कमी।

segments.src: The difference is how much you have to add.
segments.tr: अंतर केवल इतना है कि आपको कितनी मात्रा डालनी है।

segments.src: **The Big Three.** Every bag of fertilizer in the U.S.
segments.tr: **तीन बड़े तत्व (The Big Three)।** अमेरिका में उर्वरक का हर बैग

segments.src: carries three numbers on the front — say, `10-10-10`.
segments.tr: सामने की तरफ तीन नंबर दिखाता है — जैसे, `10-10-10`।

segments.src: That's the guaranteed analysis: percent nitrogen, percent phosphate (P₂O₅), percent potash (K₂O), by weight.
segments.tr: यह गारंटीकृत विश्लेषण है: नाइट्रोजन का प्रतिशत, फास्फेट (P₂O₅) का प्रतिशत, पोटाश (K₂O) का प्रतिशत, वजन के अनुसार।

segments.src: A 50 lb bag of 10-10-10 contains 5 lb of N, 5 lb of phosphate, and 5 lb of potash.
segments.tr: 10-10-10 के 50 पाउंड के बैग में 5 पाउंड N, 5 पाउंड फास्फेट और 5 पाउंड पोटाश होता है।

segments.src: The rest is carrier and filler.
segments.tr: बाकी वाहक (carrier) और फिलर है।

segments.src: Roughly what each does:
segments.tr: प्रत्येक का कार्य लगभग इस प्रकार है:

segments.src: - **Nitrogen** — leaves and stems, chlorophyll, protein. Deficiency shows as pale yellowing on the *oldest* leaves first, because the plant scavenges N from old tissue and moves it to new growth.
segments.tr: - **नाइट्रोजन** — पत्तियां और तने, क्लोरोफिल, प्रोटीन। कमी सबसे पहले *पुरानी* पत्तियों पर हल्के पीलेपन के रूप में दिखाई देती है, क्योंकि पौधा पुरानी ऊतकों से N को खींचकर नई वृद्धि में ले जाता है।

segments.src: - **Phosphorus** — roots, energy transfer, flowering and seed set. Deficiency can show as dull purple-tinged leaves.
segments.tr: - **फास्फोरस** — जड़ें, ऊर्जा हस्तांतरण, फूल आना और बीज बनना। कमी सुस्त बैंगनी रंग की पत्तियों के रूप में दिखाई दे सकती है।

segments.src: - **Potassium** — water regulation, stomatal control, disease resistance, stalk strength. Deficiency often shows as scorched leaf margins.
segments.tr: - **पोटेशियम** — जल विनियमन, रंध्र नियंत्रण, रोग प्रतिरोधक क्षमता, तने की मजबूती। कमी अक्सर पत्तियों के किनारों के झुलसने के रूप में दिखाई देती है।

segments.src: **Now the part most people skip: pH.**
segments.tr: **अब वह हिस्सा जिसे ज्यादातर लोग छोड़ देते हैं: pH।**

segments.src: Soil pH is a measure of how acidic or alkaline the soil solution is, on a 0–14 scale where 7 is neutral.
segments.tr: मिट्टी का pH यह मापता है कि मिट्टी का घोल कितना अम्लीय या क्षारीय है, 0–14 के पैमाने पर जहाँ 7 तटस्थ है।

segments.src: It matters because **pH controls nutrient availability**.
segments.tr: यह मायने रखता है क्योंकि **pH पोषक तत्वों की उपलब्धता को नियंत्रित करता है**।

segments.src: You can have plenty of phosphorus in the soil and still starve the crop, because at low pH the phosphorus binds with iron and aluminum into forms roots can't take up.
segments.tr: आपकी मिट्टी में फास्फोरस भरपूर हो सकता है और फिर भी फसल भूखी रह सकती है, क्योंकि कम pH पर फास्फोरस लोहे और एल्यूमीनियम के साथ जुड़कर ऐसे रूप ले लेता है जिन्हें जड़ें ग्रहण नहीं कर सकतीं।

segments.src: At high pH it binds with calcium instead.
segments.tr: उच्च pH पर यह इसके बजाय कैल्शियम के साथ जुड़ जाता है।

segments.src: Phosphorus is most available roughly between pH 6.0 and 7.0 — which is why most field crops and garden vegetables are happiest in the pH 6.0–7.0 window.
segments.tr: फास्फोरस लगभग pH 6.0 और 7.0 के बीच सबसे अधिक उपलब्ध होता है — यही कारण है कि अधिकांश खेत की फसलें और बगीचे की सब्जियां pH 6.0–7.0 की सीमा में सबसे खुश रहती हैं।

segments.src: Iron, manganese, and zinc run the opposite way: they get *more* available as soil turns acidic.
segments.tr: लोहा, मैंगनीज और जस्ता इसके विपरीत काम करते हैं: जैसे-जैसे मिट्टी अम्लीय होती है, वे *अधिक* उपलब्ध हो जाते हैं।

segments.src: That's why azaleas and blueberries — acid-lovers — go chlorotic and yellow in alkaline soil.
segments.tr: यही कारण है कि अज़ेलिया और ब्लूबेरी — जो अम्लीय मिट्टी पसंद करते हैं — क्षारीय मिट्टी में क्लोरोटिक और पीले पड़ जाते हैं।

segments.src: They can't get iron.
segments.tr: उन्हें लोहा नहीं मिल पाता।

segments.src: **Buffering capacity** is why fixing pH is harder than it sounds.
segments.tr: **बफरिंग क्षमता (Buffering capacity)** ही कारण है कि pH को ठीक करना सुनने में जितना आसान लगता है, उससे कहीं अधिक कठिन है।

segments.src: If you add acid to distilled water, the pH plunges.
segments.tr: यदि आप आसुत जल (distilled water) में एसिड मिलाते हैं, तो pH गिर जाता है।

segments.src: Add the same acid to soil and it barely moves.
segments.tr: वही एसिड मिट्टी में मिलाएं तो यह मुश्किल से ही बदलता है।

segments.src: That resistance is buffering, and it comes from the soil's reserve of exchangeable acidity sitting on clay particles and organic matter — a large hidden pool that keeps refilling the soil solution as you neutralize it.
segments.tr: वह प्रतिरोध बफरिंग है, और यह मिट्टी के क्ले कणों और कार्बनिक पदार्थों पर मौजूद विनिमय योग्य अम्लता (exchangeable acidity) के भंडार से आता है — एक बड़ा छिपा हुआ पूल जो मिट्टी के घोल को बेअसर करते ही उसे फिर से भर देता है।

segments.src: Practical consequence: a heavy clay soil rich in organic matter needs *far more* lime to raise its pH one unit than a sandy soil does.
segments.tr: व्यावहारिक परिणाम: कार्बनिक पदार्थों से भरपूर भारी क्ले मिट्टी को pH एक इकाई बढ़ाने के लिए रेतीली मिट्टी की तुलना में *कहीं अधिक* चूने की आवश्यकता होती है।

segments.src: That's why a soil test doesn't just report pH — it reports a **buffer pH** or **lime requirement**, which is the number that actually tells you how much lime to spread.
segments.tr: यही कारण है कि मिट्टी परीक्षण केवल pH की रिपोर्ट नहीं करता — यह **बफर pH** या **चूने की आवश्यकता (lime requirement)** की रिपोर्ट करता है, जो वह संख्या है जो वास्तव में बताती है कि कितना चूना फैलाना है।

segments.src: Soil test pH   -> where you are now
segments.tr: Soil test pH   -> where you are now

segments.src: Buffer pH      -> how hard it will be to move
segments.tr: Buffer pH      -> how hard it will be to move

segments.src: Lime rate      -> tons per acre to get where you want
segments.tr: Lime rate      -> tons per acre to get where you want

segments.src: The general rules of thumb: **lime** (calcium carbonate) raises pH; **elemental sulfur** lowers it.
segments.tr: सामान्य नियम: **चूना** (कैल्शियम कार्बोनेट) pH बढ़ाता है; **तत्व सल्फर** इसे कम करता है।

segments.src: Both work slowly — months, sometimes a full season — because they depend on soil moisture, temperature, and microbial activity.
segments.tr: दोनों धीरे-धीरे काम करते हैं — महीनों, कभी-कभी एक पूरा मौसम — क्योंकि वे मिट्टी की नमी, तापमान और सूक्ष्मजीव गतिविधि पर निर्भर करते हैं।

segments.src: One more piece of vocabulary that ties it together: **cation exchange capacity (CEC)**.
segments.tr: शब्दावली का एक और टुकड़ा जो इसे जोड़ता है: **धनायन विनिमय क्षमता (cation exchange capacity - CEC)**।

segments.src: Clay and organic matter carry negative charges, and positively charged nutrients — calcium, magnesium, potassium, ammonium — stick to those sites like magnets on a fridge.
segments.tr: क्ले और कार्बनिक पदार्थों पर नकारात्मक आवेश होते हैं, और सकारात्मक रूप से आवेशित पोषक तत्व — कैल्शियम, मैग्नीशियम, पोटेशियम, अमोनियम — उन स्थानों पर फ्रिज पर लगे चुंबकों की तरह चिपक जाते हैं।

segments.src: High CEC means a soil holds a large nutrient reserve and buffers strongly.
segments.tr: उच्च CEC का मतलब है कि मिट्टी में पोषक तत्वों का एक बड़ा भंडार है और यह मजबूती से बफर करती है।

segments.src: Low CEC (sandy soil) means nutrients leach through fast.
segments.tr: कम CEC (रेतीली मिट्टी) का मतलब है कि पोषक तत्व तेजी से रिस जाते हैं।

segments.src: Same fertilizer, very different behavior.
segments.tr: एक ही उर्वरक, बहुत अलग व्यवहार।

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: Say you're in Ohio and you plant tomatoes in the same backyard bed for the third summer running.
segments.tr: मान लीजिए आप ओहियो में हैं और आप लगातार तीसरे गर्मियों के मौसम में अपने घर के पिछले बगीचे में टमाटर लगाते हैं।

segments.src: You fertilize religiously with a high-nitrogen lawn-style product because it's what's in the garage.
segments.tr: आप धार्मिक रूप से उच्च-नाइट्रोजन वाले लॉन-स्टाइल उत्पाद के साथ खाद डालते हैं क्योंकि गैरेज में वही उपलब्ध है।

segments.src: You get magnificent, dark green, four-foot vines — and almost no fruit.
segments.tr: आपको शानदार, गहरे हरे रंग की, चार फीट लंबी बेलें मिलती हैं — और लगभग कोई फल नहीं।

segments.src: That's textbook nutrient imbalance.
segments.tr: यह पोषक तत्वों के असंतुलन का पाठ्यपुस्तक उदाहरण है।

segments.src: Excess nitrogen pushes vegetative growth at the expense of flowering and fruit set.
segments.tr: अत्यधिक नाइट्रोजन फूल आने और फल लगने की कीमत पर वानस्पतिक विकास को बढ़ावा देता है।

segments.src: Meanwhile, three seasons of removing tomatoes has been quietly withdrawing potassium and phosphorus from the account with no matching deposit.
segments.tr: इस बीच, टमाटर हटाने के तीन मौसमों ने चुपचाप खाते से पोटेशियम और फास्फोरस को बिना किसी जमा राशि के निकाल लिया है।

segments.src: And in much of the eastern U.S., where rainfall gradually leaches calcium and magnesium out of the topsoil, the pH has been drifting downward year over year — possibly into the mid-5s, where phosphorus availability drops sharply.
segments.tr: और पूर्वी अमेरिका के अधिकांश हिस्सों में, जहाँ बारिश धीरे-धीरे ऊपरी मिट्टी से कैल्शियम और मैग्नीशियम को धो देती है, pH साल-दर-साल नीचे की ओर खिसक रहा है — संभवतः 5 के मध्य तक, जहाँ फास्फोरस की उपलब्धता तेजी से गिरती है।

segments.src: The fix costs less than a bag of fertilizer.
segments.tr: इसे ठीक करने की लागत उर्वरक के एक बैग से भी कम है।

segments.src: Nearly every state has a land-grant university extension service — Ohio State, Penn State, NC State, Texas A&M — running soil testing labs, typically in the $15–$25 range per sample.
segments.tr: लगभग हर राज्य में एक लैंड-ग्रांट यूनिवर्सिटी एक्सटेंशन सर्विस है — ओहियो स्टेट, पेन स्टेट, एनसी स्टेट, टेक्सास ए एंड एम — जो मिट्टी परीक्षण प्रयोगशालाएं चलाती हैं, आमतौर पर प्रति नमूना $15–$25 की सीमा में।

segments.src: You send in a composite of 10–15 cores from around the bed.
segments.tr: आप बगीचे के चारों ओर से 10–15 कोर का एक मिश्रित नमूना भेजते हैं।

segments.src: What comes back is pH, buffer pH, extractable P and K, calcium, magnesium, organic matter percentage, and CEC, plus a recommendation in pounds per 1,000 square feet.
segments.tr: जो वापस आता है वह है pH, बफर pH, निकालने योग्य P और K, कैल्शियम, मैग्नीशियम, कार्बनिक पदार्थ का प्रतिशत, और CEC, साथ ही प्रति 1,000 वर्ग फुट पाउंड में एक सिफारिश।

segments.src: If the report says pH 5.4 with a lime requirement of 50 lb per 1,000 sq ft, spreading that lime the previous fall will do more for next year's tomatoes than any amount of fertilizer applied in June.
segments.tr: यदि रिपोर्ट में pH 5.4 और 50 पाउंड प्रति 1,000 वर्ग फुट की चूने की आवश्यकता बताई गई है, तो पिछली शरद ऋतु में उस चूने को फैलाना जून में लगाए गए किसी भी उर्वरक की तुलना में अगले साल के टमाटरों के लिए अधिक फायदेमंद होगा।

segments.src: You're not adding nutrients — you're unlocking the ones already sitting there.
segments.tr: आप पोषक तत्व नहीं जोड़ रहे हैं — आप उन पोषक तत्वों को अनलॉक कर रहे हैं जो पहले से ही वहां मौजूद हैं।

segments.src: There's an environmental side too.
segments.tr: इसका एक पर्यावरणीय पहलू भी है।

segments.src: Nutrients you apply beyond what the crop can use don't vanish.
segments.tr: फसल द्वारा उपयोग किए जा सकने वाले पोषक तत्वों से अधिक जो आप डालते हैं, वे गायब नहीं होते।

segments.src: Nitrate leaches into groundwater; phosphorus runs off into surface water and feeds algal blooms.
segments.tr: नाइट्रेट भूजल में रिस जाता है; फास्फोरस सतह के पानी में बह जाता है और शैवाल के खिलने (algal blooms) को खिलाता है।

segments.src: The recurring summer blooms in Lake Erie and the hypoxic "dead zone" in the Gulf of Mexico are both driven substantially by nutrient runoff from a very large watershed.
segments.tr: लेक एरी में बार-बार होने वाले गर्मियों के खिलने और मैक्सिको की खाड़ी में हाइपोक्सिक "डेड ज़ोन" दोनों काफी हद तक एक बहुत बड़े जलक्षेत्र से पोषक तत्वों के अपवाह (runoff) से प्रेरित हैं।

segments.src: Matching the rate to the actual soil test is the single cheapest thing that helps both your yield and the water downstream.
segments.tr: वास्तविक मिट्टी परीक्षण के अनुसार दर का मिलान करना सबसे सस्ता काम है जो आपकी उपज और नीचे की ओर के पानी दोनों में मदद करता है।

segments.src: The professional framing for this is the **4Rs**: Right source, Right rate, Right time, Right place.
segments.tr: इसके लिए पेशेवर शब्दावली **4Rs** है: सही स्रोत (Right source), सही दर (Right rate), सही समय (Right time), सही जगह (Right place)।

segments.src: Pick the fertilizer form that fits, apply only what the test calls for, put it down when the crop can use it, and place it where roots will find it.
segments.tr: उर्वरक का वह रूप चुनें जो उपयुक्त हो, केवल वही डालें जो परीक्षण कहता है, इसे तब डालें जब फसल इसका उपयोग कर सके, और इसे वहां रखें जहां जड़ें इसे पा सकें।

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## 3줄 정리

segments.src: 1. Plants need 17 essential elements; N, P, and K are needed in the largest amounts, which is why every fertilizer bag carries three numbers (`N-P₂O₅-K₂O`) on the front.
segments.tr: 1. पौधों को 17 आवश्यक तत्वों की आवश्यकता होती है; N, P, और K की सबसे अधिक मात्रा में आवश्यकता होती है, यही कारण है कि हर उर्वरक बैग के सामने तीन नंबर (`N-P₂O₅-K₂O`) होते हैं।

segments.src: 2. Soil pH governs whether nutrients are chemically *available* to roots — phosphorus peaks around pH 6.0–7.0, while iron and zinc become more available as soil turns acidic.
segments.tr: 2. मिट्टी का pH यह नियंत्रित करता है कि पोषक तत्व रासायनिक रूप से जड़ों के लिए *उपलब्ध* हैं या नहीं — फास्फोरस pH 6.0–7.0 के आसपास चरम पर होता है, जबकि मिट्टी के अम्लीय होने पर लोहा और जस्ता अधिक उपलब्ध हो जाते हैं।

segments.src: 3. Buffering capacity, driven by clay and organic matter, resists pH change — so a soil test's buffer pH, not the pH alone, tells you how much lime to apply.
segments.tr: 3. बफरिंग क्षमता, जो क्ले और कार्बनिक पदार्थों द्वारा संचालित होती है, pH परिवर्तन का विरोध करती है — इसलिए मिट्टी परीक्षण का बफर pH, न कि केवल pH, आपको बताता है कि कितना चूना डालना है।

segments.src: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈
segments.tr: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈

segments.src: **Q1.** A 50 lb bag of fertilizer is labeled `10-20-10`.
How many pounds of actual phosphate (P₂O₅) does it contain?
segments.tr: इसमें वास्तविक फास्फेट (P₂O₅) के कितने पाउंड होते हैं?

segments.src: - A) 5 lb
segments.tr: - A) 5 पाउंड

segments.src: - B) 10 lb
segments.tr: - B) 10 पाउंड

segments.src: - C) 20 lb
segments.tr: - C) 20 पाउंड

segments.src: - D) 50 lb
segments.tr: - D) 50 पाउंड

segments.src: **Q2.** O/X — Two soils both test at pH 5.5, so they will both need the same amount of lime to reach pH 6.5.
segments.tr: **Q2.** सही/गलत — दो मिट्टी दोनों का परीक्षण pH 5.5 पर होता है, इसलिए उन दोनों को pH 6.5 तक पहुँचने के लिए समान मात्रा में चूने की आवश्यकता होगी।

segments.src: **Q3.** A gardener's soil has plenty of iron in it, but the plants show yellowing between the leaf veins (chlorosis).
segments.tr: **Q3.** एक माली की मिट्टी में भरपूर लोहा है, लेकिन पौधों की पत्तियों की नसों के बीच पीलापन (क्लोरोसिस) दिखाई देता है।

segments.src: Which condition is the most likely cause?
segments.tr: कौन सी स्थिति सबसे संभावित कारण है?

segments.src: - A) Soil pH is too low (strongly acidic)
segments.tr: - A) मिट्टी का pH बहुत कम है (अत्यधिक अम्लीय)

segments.src: - B) Soil pH is too high (alkaline)
segments.tr: - B) मिट्टी का pH बहुत अधिक है (क्षारीय)

segments.src: - C) Nitrogen was over-applied
segments.tr: - C) नाइट्रोजन का अत्यधिक उपयोग किया गया था

segments.src: - D) The soil has no cation exchange capacity
segments.tr: - D) मिट्टी में कोई धनायन विनिमय क्षमता नहीं है

segments.src: ## 📚 오늘의 용어
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Essential element** — A nutrient a plant cannot complete its life cycle without, and whose role no other element can substitute for; there are 17.
segments.tr: - **आवश्यक तत्व (Essential element)** — एक पोषक तत्व जिसके बिना पौधा अपना जीवन चक्र पूरा नहीं कर सकता, और जिसकी भूमिका कोई अन्य तत्व प्रतिस्थापित नहीं कर सकता; ऐसे 17 तत्व हैं।

segments.src: - **Macronutrient / Micronutrient** — Classification by the *amount* a plant needs, not by importance; both categories are equally essential.
segments.tr: - **मैक्रोन्यूट्रिएंट / माइक्रोन्यूट्रिएंट** — पौधे की *आवश्यकता की मात्रा* के आधार पर वर्गीकरण, न कि महत्व के आधार पर; दोनों श्रेणियां समान रूप से आवश्यक हैं।

segments.src: - **Guaranteed analysis (N-P-K)** — The three numbers on a fertilizer label giving percent nitrogen, percent phosphate (P₂O₅), and percent potash (K₂O) by weight.
segments.tr: - **गारंटीकृत विश्लेषण (N-P-K)** — उर्वरक लेबल पर तीन नंबर जो वजन के अनुसार नाइट्रोजन प्रतिशत, फास्फेट (P₂O₅) प्रतिशत और पोटाश (K₂O) प्रतिशत देते हैं।

segments.src: - **Soil pH** — The acidity or alkalinity of the soil solution on a 0–14 scale; it determines the chemical form, and therefore the availability, of most nutrients.
segments.tr: - **मिट्टी का pH** — 0–14 के पैमाने पर मिट्टी के घोल की अम्लता या क्षारीयता; यह अधिकांश पोषक तत्वों के रासायनिक रूप और इसलिए उनकी उपलब्धता को निर्धारित करता है।

segments.src: - **Buffering capacity** — A soil's resistance to pH change, supplied by exchangeable acidity held on clay and organic matter; it sets how much lime or sulfur is actually required.
segments.tr: - **बफरिंग क्षमता** — pH परिवर्तन के प्रति मिट्टी का प्रतिरोध, जो क्ले और कार्बनिक पदार्थों पर मौजूद विनिमय योग्य अम्लता द्वारा प्रदान किया जाता है; यह निर्धारित करता है कि वास्तव में कितना चूना या सल्फर आवश्यक है।

segments.src: - **Cation exchange capacity (CEC)** — The soil's total capacity to hold positively charged nutrients on negatively charged clay and organic matter surfaces; a proxy for nutrient-holding ability.
segments.tr: - **धनायन विनिमय क्षमता (CEC)** — नकारात्मक रूप से आवेशित क्ले और कार्बनिक पदार्थ की सतहों पर सकारात्मक रूप से आवेशित पोषक तत्वों को रखने की मिट्टी की कुल क्षमता; पोषक तत्वों को धारण करने की क्षमता का एक प्रॉक्सी।

segments.src: *정답: **Q1 → B (10 lb).** The middle number is percent by weight, so 20% of 50 lb = 10 lb of phosphate.
segments.tr: *उत्तर: **Q1 → B (10 पाउंड)।** बीच की संख्या वजन के अनुसार प्रतिशत है, इसलिए 50 पाउंड का 20% = 10 पाउंड फास्फेट।

segments.src: Note this is P₂O₅, the oxide form used on labels, not elemental phosphorus — elemental P would be about 44% of that figure.*
segments.tr: ध्यान दें कि यह P₂O₅ है, लेबल पर उपयोग किया जाने वाला ऑक्साइड रूप, न कि मौलिक फास्फोरस — मौलिक P उस आंकड़े का लगभग 44% होगा।*

segments.src: ***Q2 → X (False).** Identical pH does not mean identical lime requirement.
segments.tr: ***Q2 → X (गलत)।** समान pH का मतलब समान चूने की आवश्यकता नहीं है।

segments.src: A heavy clay soil high in organic matter has a large reserve of exchangeable acidity — high buffering — and may need several times the lime a sandy soil needs to make the same pH move.
segments.tr: कार्बनिक पदार्थों से भरपूर भारी क्ले मिट्टी में विनिमय योग्य अम्लता का एक बड़ा भंडार होता है — उच्च बफरिंग — और pH में समान बदलाव लाने के लिए इसे रेतीली मिट्टी की तुलना में कई गुना अधिक चूने की आवश्यकता हो सकती है।

segments.src: This is exactly why soil test reports include a buffer pH.*
segments.tr: यही कारण है कि मिट्टी परीक्षण रिपोर्ट में बफर pH शामिल होता है।*

segments.src: ***Q3 → B.** Iron becomes progressively less soluble as pH rises; in alkaline soil it precipitates into forms roots cannot absorb.
segments.tr: ***Q3 → B.** जैसे-जैसे pH बढ़ता है, लोहा धीरे-धीरे कम घुलनशील होता जाता है; क्षारीय मिट्टी में यह ऐसे रूपों में अवक्षेपित हो जाता है जिन्हें जड़ें अवशोषित नहीं कर सकतीं।

segments.src: The plant is iron-deficient despite iron being physically present — a good illustration that total nutrient content and plant-available nutrient content are two different things.
segments.tr: लोहा भौतिक रूप से मौजूद होने के बावजूद पौधा लोहे की कमी से ग्रस्त है — यह एक अच्छा उदाहरण है कि कुल पोषक तत्व सामग्री और पौधे के लिए उपलब्ध पोषक तत्व सामग्री दो अलग-अलग चीजें हैं।

segments.src: Interveinal chlorosis on the youngest leaves is the classic symptom, because iron is not readily remobilized within the plant.*
segments.tr: सबसे नई पत्तियों पर इंटरवेनल क्लोरोसिस (नसों के बीच पीलापन) क्लासिक लक्षण है, क्योंकि लोहा पौधे के भीतर आसानी से पुनर्गठित नहीं होता है।*

es.title: [Agriculture 101 #4] Tu suelo es una cuenta bancaria: así es como funcionan los depósitos y retiros

segments.src: > Plants need 17 essential elements, but three of them (N, P, K) do most of the heavy lifting — and soil pH quietly decides how much of any of them a root can actually reach.
segments.tr: > Las plantas necesitan 17 elementos esenciales, pero tres de ellos (N, P, K) hacen la mayor parte del trabajo pesado, y el pH del suelo determina silenciosamente cuánto de cualquiera de ellos puede alcanzar realmente una raíz.

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Think of soil as a checking account that plants draw from every day.
segments.tr: Piensa en el suelo como una cuenta corriente de la que las plantas retiran fondos todos los días.

segments.src: Plants build themselves out of **essential elements** — nutrients that, if missing, mean the plant literally cannot complete its life cycle.
segments.tr: Las plantas se construyen a partir de **elementos esenciales**, nutrientes que, si faltan, significan que la planta literalmente no puede completar su ciclo de vida.

segments.src: There are 17 of them.
segments.tr: Hay 17 de ellos.

segments.src: Three come free from air and water: carbon, hydrogen, oxygen.
segments.tr: Tres provienen gratis del aire y del agua: carbono, hidrógeno, oxígeno.

segments.src: The other 14 come from the soil.
segments.tr: Los otros 14 provienen del suelo.

segments.src: Those 14 split into two groups by *quantity needed*, not importance:
segments.tr: Esos 14 se dividen en dos grupos según la *cantidad necesaria*, no la importancia:

segments.src: - **Macronutrients** (needed in large amounts): nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), plus calcium, magnesium, and sulfur.
segments.tr: - **Macronutrientes** (necesarios en grandes cantidades): nitrógeno (N), fósforo (P), potasio (K), además de calcio, magnesio y azufre.

segments.src: - **Micronutrients** (needed in trace amounts): iron, manganese, zinc, copper, boron, molybdenum, chlorine, nickel.
segments.tr: - **Micronutrientes** (necesarios en cantidades traza): hierro, manganeso, zinc, cobre, boro, molibdeno, cloro, níquel.

segments.src: A micronutrient deficiency will kill a crop just as dead as a nitrogen shortage.
segments.tr: Una deficiencia de micronutrientes matará a un cultivo de la misma manera que la escasez de nitrógeno.

segments.src: The difference is how much you have to add.
segments.tr: La diferencia es cuánto tienes que añadir.

segments.src: **The Big Three.** Every bag of fertilizer in the U.S.
segments.tr: **Los Tres Grandes.** Cada bolsa de fertilizante en EE. UU.

segments.src: carries three numbers on the front — say, `10-10-10`.
segments.tr: lleva tres números en el frente, por ejemplo, `10-10-10`.

segments.src: That's the guaranteed analysis: percent nitrogen, percent phosphate (P₂O₅), percent potash (K₂O), by weight.
segments.tr: Ese es el análisis garantizado: porcentaje de nitrógeno, porcentaje de fosfato (P₂O₅), porcentaje de potasa (K₂O), en peso.

segments.src: A 50 lb bag of 10-10-10 contains 5 lb of N, 5 lb of phosphate, and 5 lb of potash.
segments.tr: Una bolsa de 50 lb de 10-10-10 contiene 5 lb de N, 5 lb de fosfato y 5 lb de potasa.

segments.src: The rest is carrier and filler.
segments.tr: El resto es portador y relleno.

segments.src: Roughly what each does:
segments.tr: Más o menos lo que hace cada uno:

segments.src: - **Nitrogen** — leaves and stems, chlorophyll, protein. Deficiency shows as pale yellowing on the *oldest* leaves first, because the plant scavenges N from old tissue and moves it to new growth.
segments.tr: - **Nitrógeno**: hojas y tallos, clorofila, proteína. La deficiencia se muestra como un amarillamiento pálido en las hojas *más viejas* primero, porque la planta toma N del tejido viejo y lo mueve hacia el nuevo crecimiento.

segments.src: - **Phosphorus** — roots, energy transfer, flowering and seed set. Deficiency can show as dull purple-tinged leaves.
segments.tr: - **Fósforo**: raíces, transferencia de energía, floración y formación de semillas. La deficiencia puede mostrarse como hojas opacas con matices púrpuras.

segments.src: - **Potassium** — water regulation, stomatal control, disease resistance, stalk strength. Deficiency often shows as scorched leaf margins.
segments.tr: - **Potasio**: regulación del agua, control estomático, resistencia a enfermedades, fuerza del tallo. La deficiencia a menudo se muestra como márgenes de las hojas quemados.

segments.src: **Now the part most people skip: pH.**
segments.tr: **Ahora la parte que la mayoría se salta: el pH.**

segments.src: Soil pH is a measure of how acidic or alkaline the soil solution is, on a 0–14 scale where 7 is neutral.
segments.tr: El pH del suelo es una medida de qué tan ácida o alcalina es la solución del suelo, en una escala de 0 a 14 donde 7 es neutro.

segments.src: It matters because **pH controls nutrient availability**.
segments.tr: Importa porque **el pH controla la disponibilidad de nutrientes**.

segments.src: You can have plenty of phosphorus in the soil and still starve the crop, because at low pH the phosphorus binds with iron and aluminum into forms roots can't take up.
segments.tr: Puedes tener mucho fósforo en el suelo y aun así hacer pasar hambre al cultivo, porque a un pH bajo el fósforo se une con el hierro y el aluminio en formas que las raíces no pueden absorber.

segments.src: At high pH it binds with calcium instead.
segments.tr: A un pH alto se une con el calcio en su lugar.

segments.src: Phosphorus is most available roughly between pH 6.0 and 7.0 — which is why most field crops and garden vegetables are happiest in the pH 6.0–7.0 window.
segments.tr: El fósforo está más disponible aproximadamente entre pH 6.0 y 7.0, razón por la cual la mayoría de los cultivos de campo y hortalizas de jardín son más felices en la ventana de pH 6.0–7.0.

segments.src: Iron, manganese, and zinc run the opposite way: they get *more* available as soil turns acidic.
segments.tr: El hierro, el manganeso y el zinc funcionan al revés: se vuelven *más* disponibles a medida que el suelo se vuelve ácido.

segments.src: That's why azaleas and blueberries — acid-lovers — go chlorotic and yellow in alkaline soil.
segments.tr: Es por eso que las azaleas y los arándanos, amantes de los ácidos, se vuelven cloróticos y amarillos en suelos alcalinos.

segments.src: They can't get iron.
segments.tr: No pueden conseguir hierro.

segments.src: **Buffering capacity** is why fixing pH is harder than it sounds.
segments.tr: La **capacidad amortiguadora** es la razón por la cual arreglar el pH es más difícil de lo que parece.

segments.src: If you add acid to distilled water, the pH plunges.
segments.tr: Si añades ácido a agua destilada, el pH se desploma.

segments.src: Add the same acid to soil and it barely moves.
segments.tr: Añade el mismo ácido al suelo y apenas se mueve.

segments.src: That resistance is buffering, and it comes from the soil's reserve of exchangeable acidity sitting on clay particles and organic matter — a large hidden pool that keeps refilling the soil solution as you neutralize it.
segments.tr: Esa resistencia es la amortiguación, y proviene de la reserva de acidez intercambiable del suelo situada en las partículas de arcilla y materia orgánica, una gran reserva oculta que sigue rellenando la solución del suelo a medida que la neutralizas.

segments.src: Practical consequence: a heavy clay soil rich in organic matter needs *far more* lime to raise its pH one unit than a sandy soil does.
segments.tr: Consecuencia práctica: un suelo arcilloso pesado rico en materia orgánica necesita *mucho más* cal para elevar su pH una unidad que un suelo arenoso.

segments.src: That's why a soil test doesn't just report pH — it reports a **buffer pH** or **lime requirement**, which is the number that actually tells you how much lime to spread.
segments.tr: Es por eso que una prueba de suelo no solo informa el pH, sino que informa un **pH tampón** o **requerimiento de cal**, que es el número que realmente te dice cuánta cal esparcir.

segments.src: Soil test pH   -> where you are now
segments.tr: Soil test pH   -> where you are now

segments.src: Buffer pH      -> how hard it will be to move
segments.tr: Buffer pH      -> how hard it will be to move

segments.src: Lime rate      -> tons per acre to get where you want
segments.tr: Lime rate      -> tons per acre to get where you want

segments.src: The general rules of thumb: **lime** (calcium carbonate) raises pH; **elemental sulfur** lowers it.
segments.tr: Las reglas generales habituales: la **cal** (carbonato de calcio) eleva el pH; el **azufre elemental** lo baja.

segments.src: Both work slowly — months, sometimes a full season — because they depend on soil moisture, temperature, and microbial activity.
segments.tr: Ambos funcionan lentamente (meses, a veces una temporada completa) porque dependen de la humedad del suelo, la temperatura y la actividad microbiana.

segments.src: One more piece of vocabulary that ties it together: **cation exchange capacity (CEC)**.
segments.tr: Una pieza más de vocabulario que une todo: la **capacidad de intercambio catiónico (CIC)**.

segments.src: Clay and organic matter carry negative charges, and positively charged nutrients — calcium, magnesium, potassium, ammonium — stick to those sites like magnets on a fridge.
segments.tr: La arcilla y la materia orgánica llevan cargas negativas, y los nutrientes cargados positivamente (calcio, magnesio, potasio, amonio) se adhieren a esos sitios como imanes en un refrigerador.

segments.src: High CEC means a soil holds a large nutrient reserve and buffers strongly.
segments.tr: Una CIC alta significa que un suelo retiene una gran reserva de nutrientes y se amortigua fuertemente.

segments.src: Low CEC (sandy soil) means nutrients leach through fast.
segments.tr: Una CIC baja (suelo arenoso) significa que los nutrientes se lixivian rápidamente.

segments.src: Same fertilizer, very different behavior.
segments.tr: Mismo fertilizante, comportamiento muy diferente.

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: Say you're in Ohio and you plant tomatoes in the same backyard bed for the third summer running.
segments.tr: Digamos que estás en Ohio y plantas tomates en el mismo bancal del patio trasero por tercer verano consecutivo.

segments.src: You fertilize religiously with a high-nitrogen lawn-style product because it's what's in the garage.
segments.tr: Fertilizas religiosamente con un producto estilo césped alto en nitrógeno porque es lo que hay en el garaje.

segments.src: You get magnificent, dark green, four-foot vines — and almost no fruit.
segments.tr: Obtienes enredaderas magníficas, de verde oscuro y de cuatro pies, y casi nada de fruta.

segments.src: That's textbook nutrient imbalance.
segments.tr: Eso es un desequilibrio de nutrientes de libro de texto.

segments.src: Excess nitrogen pushes vegetative growth at the expense of flowering and fruit set.
segments.tr: El exceso de nitrógeno impulsa el crecimiento vegetativo a expensas de la floración y el cuajado de frutos.

segments.src: Meanwhile, three seasons of removing tomatoes has been quietly withdrawing potassium and phosphorus from the account with no matching deposit.
segments.tr: Mientras tanto, tres temporadas de extracción de tomates han estado retirando silenciosamente potasio y fósforo de la cuenta sin un depósito correspondiente.

segments.src: And in much of the eastern U.S., where rainfall gradually leaches calcium and magnesium out of the topsoil, the pH has been drifting downward year over year — possibly into the mid-5s, where phosphorus availability drops sharply.
segments.tr: Y en gran parte del este de EE. UU., donde las precipitaciones lixivian gradualmente el calcio y el magnesio de la capa superior del suelo, el pH ha estado bajando año tras año, posiblemente hacia la mitad de los 5, donde la disponibilidad de fósforo cae drásticamente.

segments.src: The fix costs less than a bag of fertilizer.
segments.tr: La solución cuesta menos que una bolsa de fertilizante.

segments.src: Nearly every state has a land-grant university extension service — Ohio State, Penn State, NC State, Texas A&M — running soil testing labs, typically in the $15–$25 range per sample.
segments.tr: Casi todos los estados tienen un servicio de extensión universitaria con concesión de tierras (Ohio State, Penn State, NC State, Texas A&M) que administra laboratorios de análisis de suelos, típicamente en el rango de $15–$25 por muestra.

segments.src: You send in a composite of 10–15 cores from around the bed.
segments.tr: Envías un compuesto de 10 a 15 núcleos de alrededor del lecho.

segments.src: What comes back is pH, buffer pH, extractable P and K, calcium, magnesium, organic matter percentage, and CEC, plus a recommendation in pounds per 1,000 square feet.
segments.tr: Lo que regresa es el pH, el pH tampón, P y K extraíbles, calcio, magnesio, porcentaje de materia orgánica y CIC, además de una recomendación en libras por 1,000 pies cuadrados.

segments.src: If the report says pH 5.4 with a lime requirement of 50 lb per 1,000 sq ft, spreading that lime the previous fall will do more for next year's tomatoes than any amount of fertilizer applied in June.
segments.tr: Si el informe dice pH 5.4 con un requerimiento de cal de 50 lb por 1,000 pies cuadrados, esparcir esa cal el otoño anterior hará más por los tomates del próximo año que cualquier cantidad de fertilizante aplicado en junio.

segments.src: You're not adding nutrients — you're unlocking the ones already sitting there.
segments.tr: No estás añadiendo nutrientes, estás desbloqueando los que ya están allí.

segments.src: There's an environmental side too.
segments.tr: También hay un lado ambiental.

segments.src: Nutrients you apply beyond what the crop can use don't vanish.
segments.tr: Los nutrientes que aplicas más allá de lo que el cultivo puede usar no desaparecen.

segments.src: Nitrate leaches into groundwater; phosphorus runs off into surface water and feeds algal blooms.
segments.tr: El nitrato se filtra en las aguas subterráneas; el fósforo llega a las aguas superficiales y alimenta la proliferación de algas.

segments.src: The recurring summer blooms in Lake Erie and the hypoxic "dead zone" in the Gulf of Mexico are both driven substantially by nutrient runoff from a very large watershed.
segments.tr: Las floraciones estivales recurrentes en el lago Erie y la "zona muerta" hipóxica en el Golfo de México son impulsadas sustancialmente por la escorrentía de nutrientes de una cuenca hidrográfica muy grande.

segments.src: Matching the rate to the actual soil test is the single cheapest thing that helps both your yield and the water downstream.
segments.tr: Hacer coincidir la tasa con la prueba de suelo real es lo más barato que ayuda tanto a tu rendimiento como al agua río abajo.

segments.src: The professional framing for this is the **4Rs**: Right source, Right rate, Right time, Right place.
segments.tr: El marco profesional para esto son las **4R**: Fuente correcta, Tasa correcta, Momento correcto, Lugar correcto.

segments.src: Pick the fertilizer form that fits, apply only what the test calls for, put it down when the crop can use it, and place it where roots will find it.
segments.tr: Elige la forma de fertilizante que se adapte, aplica solo lo que requiere la prueba, colócalo cuando el cultivo pueda usarlo y ubícalo donde las raíces lo encuentren.

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## 3줄 정리

segments.src: 1. Plants need 17 essential elements; N, P, and K are needed in the largest amounts, which is why every fertilizer bag carries three numbers (`N-P₂O₅-K₂O`) on the front.
segments.tr: 1. Las plantas necesitan 17 elementos esenciales; N, P y K se necesitan en las mayores cantidades, razón por la cual cada bolsa de fertilizante lleva tres números (`N-P₂O₅-K₂O`) en el frente.

segments.src: 2. Soil pH governs whether nutrients are chemically *available* to roots — phosphorus peaks around pH 6.0–7.0, while iron and zinc become more available as soil turns acidic.
segments.tr: 2. El pH del suelo rige si los nutrientes están químicamente *disponibles* para las raíces; el fósforo alcanza su punto máximo alrededor de pH 6.0–7.0, mientras que el hierro y el zinc se vuelven más disponibles a medida que el suelo se vuelve ácido.

segments.src: 3. Buffering capacity, driven by clay and organic matter, resists pH change — so a soil test's buffer pH, not the pH alone, tells you how much lime to apply.
segments.tr: 3. La capacidad de amortiguación, impulsada por la arcilla y la materia orgánica, se resiste al cambio de pH, por lo que el pH tampón de una prueba de suelo, y no solo el pH, te dice cuánta cal aplicar.

segments.src: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈
segments.tr: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈

segments.src: **Q1.** A 50 lb bag of fertilizer is labeled `10-20-10`.
segments.tr: **Q1.** Una bolsa de 50 lb de fertilizante está etiquetada como `10-20-10`.

segments.src: How many pounds of actual phosphate (P₂O₅) does it contain?
segments.tr: ¿Cuántas libras de fosfato real (P₂O₅) contiene?

segments.src: - A) 5 lb
segments.tr: - A) 5 lb

segments.src: - B) 10 lb
segments.tr: - B) 10 lb

segments.src: - C) 20 lb
segments.tr: - C) 20 lb

segments.src: - D) 50 lb
segments.tr: - D) 50 lb

segments.src: **Q2.** O/X — Two soils both test at pH 5.5, so they will both need the same amount of lime to reach pH 6.5.
segments.tr: **Q2.** V/F — Dos suelos se analizan ambos a pH 5.5, por lo que ambos necesitarán la misma cantidad de cal para alcanzar un pH de 6.5.

segments.src: **Q3.** A gardener's soil has plenty of iron in it, but the plants show yellowing between the leaf veins (chlorosis).
segments.tr: **Q3.** El suelo de un jardinero tiene mucho hierro, pero las plantas muestran un amarillamiento entre las venas de las hojas (clorosis).

segments.src: Which condition is the most likely cause?
segments.tr: ¿Qué condición es la causa más probable?

segments.src: - A) Soil pH is too low (strongly acidic)
segments.tr: - A) El pH del suelo es demasiado bajo (fuertemente ácido)

segments.src: - B) Soil pH is too high (alkaline)
segments.tr: - B) El pH del suelo es demasiado alto (alcalino)

segments.src: - C) Nitrogen was over-applied
segments.tr: - C) Se aplicó demasiado nitrógeno

segments.src: - D) The soil has no cation exchange capacity
segments.tr: - D) El suelo no tiene capacidad de intercambio catiónico

segments.src: ## 📚 오늘의 용어
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Essential element** — A nutrient a plant cannot complete its life cycle without, and whose role no other element can substitute for; there are 17.
segments.tr: - **Elemento esencial**: un nutriente sin el cual una planta no puede completar su ciclo de vida y cuyo papel ningún otro elemento puede sustituir; hay 17.

segments.src: - **Macronutrient / Micronutrient** — Classification by the *amount* a plant needs, not by importance; both categories are equally essential.
segments.tr: - **Macronutriente / Micronutriente**: clasificación por la *cantidad* que necesita una planta, no por importancia; ambas categorías son igualmente esenciales.

segments.src: - **Guaranteed analysis (N-P-K)** — The three numbers on a fertilizer label giving percent nitrogen, percent phosphate (P₂O₅), and percent potash (K₂O) by weight.
segments.tr: - **Análisis garantizado (N-P-K)**: los tres números en una etiqueta de fertilizante que indican el porcentaje de nitrógeno, el porcentaje de fosfato (P₂O₅) y el porcentaje de potasa (K₂O) en peso.

segments.src: - **Soil pH** — The acidity or alkalinity of the soil solution on a 0–14 scale; it determines the chemical form, and therefore the availability, of most nutrients.
segments.tr: - **pH del suelo**: la acidez o alcalinidad de la solución del suelo en una escala de 0 a 14; determina la forma química y, por lo tanto, la disponibilidad de la mayoría de los nutrientes.

segments.src: - **Buffering capacity** — A soil's resistance to pH change, supplied by exchangeable acidity held on clay and organic matter; it sets how much lime or sulfur is actually required.
segments.tr: - **Capacidad amortiguadora**: la resistencia de un suelo al cambio de pH, proporcionada por la acidez intercambiable retenida en la arcilla y la materia orgánica; establece cuánta cal o azufre se requiere realmente.

segments.src: - **Cation exchange capacity (CEC)** — The soil's total capacity to hold positively charged nutrients on negatively charged clay and organic matter surfaces; a proxy for nutrient-holding ability.
segments.tr: - **Capacidad de intercambio catiónico (CIC)**: la capacidad total del suelo para retener nutrientes cargados positivamente en superficies de arcilla y materia orgánica cargadas negativamente; un indicador de la capacidad de retención de nutrientes.

segments.src: *정답: **Q1 → B (10 lb).** The middle number is percent by weight, so 20% of 50 lb = 10 lb of phosphate.
segments.tr: *Respuesta: **Q1 → B (10 lb).** El número del medio es el porcentaje en peso, por lo que el 20% de 50 lb = 10 lb de fosfato.

segments.src: Note this is P₂O₅, the oxide form used on labels, not elemental phosphorus — elemental P would be about 44% of that figure.*
segments.tr: Tenga en cuenta que esto es P₂O₅, la forma de óxido utilizada en las etiquetas, no fósforo elemental; el P elemental sería aproximadamente el 44% de esa cifra.*

segments.src: ***Q2 → X (False).** Identical pH does not mean identical lime requirement.
segments.tr: ***Q2 → F (Falso).** Un pH idéntico no significa un requisito de cal idéntico.

segments.src: A heavy clay soil high in organic matter has a large reserve of exchangeable acidity — high buffering — and may need several times the lime a sandy soil needs to make the same pH move.
segments.tr: Un suelo arcilloso pesado con alto contenido de materia orgánica tiene una gran reserva de acidez intercambiable (alta amortiguación) y puede necesitar varias veces la cal que necesita un suelo arenoso para hacer el mismo cambio de pH.

segments.src: This is exactly why soil test reports include a buffer pH.*
segments.tr: Esto es exactamente por qué los informes de análisis de suelos incluyen un pH tampón.*

segments.src: ***Q3 → B.** Iron becomes progressively less soluble as pH rises; in alkaline soil it precipitates into forms roots cannot absorb.
segments.tr: ***Q3 → B.** El hierro se vuelve progresivamente menos soluble a medida que el pH aumenta; en suelo alcalino precipita en formas que las raíces no pueden absorber.

segments.src: The plant is iron-deficient despite iron being physically present — a good illustration that total nutrient content and plant-available nutrient content are two different things.
segments.tr: La planta es deficiente en hierro a pesar de que el hierro está físicamente presente, una buena ilustración de que el contenido total de nutrientes y el contenido de nutrientes disponible para las plantas son dos cosas diferentes.

segments.src: Interveinal chlorosis on the youngest leaves is the classic symptom, because iron is not readily remobilized within the plant.*
segments.tr: La clorosis intervenal en las hojas más jóvenes es el síntoma clásico, porque el hierro no se moviliza fácilmente dentro de la planta.*
