segments.src: > Plants need 17 essential elements, but three of them (N, P, K) do most of the heavy lifting — and soil pH quietly decides how much of any of them a root can actually reach.
segments.tr: > 植物には17の必須元素が必要ですが、そのうちの3つ（N、P、K）が大部分を担っており、土壌のpHが、その中のどれを根が実際にどのくらい吸収できるかを静かに決定しています。

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Think of soil as a checking account that plants draw from every day.
segments.tr: 土壌を、植物が毎日引き出す当座預金口座と考えてみてください。

segments.src: Plants build themselves out of **essential elements** — nutrients that, if missing, mean the plant literally cannot complete its life cycle.
segments.tr: 植物は**必須元素**、つまり、もし欠けていれば植物が文字通りライフサイクルを完了できなくなる栄養素から自らを構築しています。

segments.src: There are 17 of them.
segments.tr: それらは17種類あります。

segments.src: Three come free from air and water: carbon, hydrogen, oxygen.
segments.tr: 3つは空気と水から無料で得られます：炭素、水素、酸素。

segments.src: The other 14 come from the soil.
segments.tr: 残りの14個は土壌から得られます。

segments.src: Those 14 split into two groups by *quantity needed*, not importance:
segments.tr: その14個は、重要性ではなく*必要な量*によって2つのグループに分かれます：

segments.src: - **Macronutrients** (needed in large amounts): nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), plus calcium, magnesium, and sulfur.
segments.tr: - **多量要素**（大量に必要なもの）：窒素（N）、リン（P）、カリウム（K）、およびカルシウム、マグネシウム、硫黄。

segments.src: - **Micronutrients** (needed in trace amounts): iron, manganese, zinc, copper, boron, molybdenum, chlorine, nickel.
segments.tr: - **微量要素**（微量で足りるもの）：鉄、マンガン、亜鉛、銅、ホウ素、モリブデン、塩素、ニッケル。

segments.src: A micronutrient deficiency will kill a crop just as dead as a nitrogen shortage.
segments.tr: 微量要素の欠乏は、窒素不足と同じくらい確実に作物を枯らします。

segments.src: The difference is how much you have to add.
segments.tr: 違いは、どれだけ添加しなければならないかだけです。

segments.src: **The Big Three.** Every bag of fertilizer in the U.S.
segments.tr: **三大栄養素。** 米国のすべての肥料の袋の

segments.src: carries three numbers on the front — say, `10-10-10`.
segments.tr: 表面には3つの数字が書かれています — 例えば、`10-10-10`のように。

segments.src: That's the guaranteed analysis: percent nitrogen, percent phosphate (P₂O₅), percent potash (K₂O), by weight.
segments.tr: これが保証成分量で、重量あたりの窒素のパーセント、リン酸（P₂O₅）のパーセント、カリ（K₂O）のパーセントです。

segments.src: A 50 lb bag of 10-10-10 contains 5 lb of N, 5 lb of phosphate, and 5 lb of potash.
segments.tr: 10-10-10の50ポンドの袋には、5ポンドのN、5ポンドのリン酸、5ポンドのカリが含まれています。

segments.src: The rest is carrier and filler.
segments.tr: 残りはキャリアとフィラーです。

segments.src: Roughly what each does:
segments.tr: それぞれが果たすおおまかな役割：

segments.src: - **Nitrogen** — leaves and stems, chlorophyll, protein. Deficiency shows as pale yellowing on the *oldest* leaves first, because the plant scavenges N from old tissue and moves it to new growth.
segments.tr: - **窒素** — 葉と茎、葉緑素、タンパク質。植物が古い組織からNを回収して新しい成長へ移動させるため、欠乏症は*最も古い*葉の淡い黄変として最初に現れます。

segments.src: - **Phosphorus** — roots, energy transfer, flowering and seed set. Deficiency can show as dull purple-tinged leaves.
segments.tr: - **リン** — 根、エネルギー伝達、開花と結実。欠乏症は鈍い紫色がかった葉として現れることがあります。

segments.src: - **Potassium** — water regulation, stomatal control, disease resistance, stalk strength. Deficiency often shows as scorched leaf margins.
segments.tr: - **カリウム** — 水分調節、気孔制御、耐病性、茎の強度。欠乏症はしばしば葉の縁の枯れ込みとして現れます。

segments.src: **Now the part most people skip: pH.**
segments.tr: **ここからがほとんどの人が飛ばす部分：pH。**

segments.src: Soil pH is a measure of how acidic or alkaline the soil solution is, on a 0–14 scale where 7 is neutral.
segments.tr: 土壌pHは、7を中性とする0〜14のスケールで、土壌溶液がどれほど酸性かアルカリ性かを示す尺度です。

segments.src: It matters because **pH controls nutrient availability**.
segments.tr: それが重要なのは、**pHが養分可給性を制御している**からです。

segments.src: You can have plenty of phosphorus in the soil and still starve the crop, because at low pH the phosphorus binds with iron and aluminum into forms roots can't take up.
segments.tr: 土壌にリンが豊富にあっても作物を飢えさせることがあり得ます。なぜなら、低いpHではリンが鉄やアルミニウムと結合して根が吸収できない形態になってしまうからです。

segments.src: At high pH it binds with calcium instead.
segments.tr: 高いpHでは、代わりにカルシウムと結合します。

segments.src: Phosphorus is most available roughly between pH 6.0 and 7.0 — which is why most field crops and garden vegetables are happiest in the pH 6.0–7.0 window.
segments.tr: リンが最も利用しやすくなるのはおおむねpH 6.0から7.0の間であり — だからこそほとんどの畑作物や庭の野菜はpH 6.0〜7.0の窓で最もよく育ちます。

segments.src: Iron, manganese, and zinc run the opposite way: they get *more* available as soil turns acidic.
segments.tr: 鉄、マンガン、亜鉛は逆の動きをします。土壌が酸性化するにつれて*より*利用しやすくなります。

segments.src: That's why azaleas and blueberries — acid-lovers — go chlorotic and yellow in alkaline soil.
segments.tr: だからこそ、酸性を好むツツジやブルーベリーは、アルカリ性土壌でクロロシスを起こして黄色くなるのです。

segments.src: They can't get iron.
segments.tr: 鉄を摂取できないからです。

segments.src: **Buffering capacity** is why fixing pH is harder than it sounds.
segments.tr: **緩衝能**があるため、pHを修正することは聞こえるほど簡単ではありません。

segments.src: If you add acid to distilled water, the pH plunges.
segments.tr: 蒸留水に酸を加えると、pHは急落します。

segments.src: Add the same acid to soil and it barely moves.
segments.tr: 同じ酸を土壌に加えても、ほとんど動きません。

segments.src: That resistance is buffering, and it comes from the soil's reserve of exchangeable acidity sitting on clay particles and organic matter — a large hidden pool that keeps refilling the soil solution as you neutralize it.
segments.tr: その抵抗力が緩衝能であり、粘土粒子や有機物に付着している交換可能酸度の土壌の備えから生じています — 中和するにつれて土壌溶液を補充し続ける、大きく隠されたプールです。

segments.src: Practical consequence: a heavy clay soil rich in organic matter needs *far more* lime to raise its pH one unit than a sandy soil does.
segments.tr: 実践的な結果：有機物が豊富な重い粘土質の土壌は、砂質土壌よりも、pHを1単位上げるために*はるかに多くの*石灰を必要とします。

segments.src: That's why a soil test doesn't just report pH — it reports a **buffer pH** or **lime requirement**, which is the number that actually tells you how much lime to spread.
segments.tr: だからこそ、土壌検査はpHを報告するだけでなく — **緩衝pH**や**石灰要求量**を報告します。これは実際にどれだけの石灰を散布すべきかを教えてくれる数値です。

segments.src: Soil test pH   -> where you are now
segments.tr: Soil test pH   -> where you are now

segments.src: Buffer pH      -> how hard it will be to move
segments.tr: Buffer pH      -> how hard it will be to move

segments.src: Lime rate      -> tons per acre to get where you want
segments.tr: Lime rate      -> tons per acre to get where you want

segments.src: The general rules of thumb: **lime** (calcium carbonate) raises pH; **elemental sulfur** lowers it.
segments.tr: 一般的な経験則：**石灰**（炭酸カルシウム）はpHを上げ、**元素状硫黄**はpHを下げます。

segments.src: Both work slowly — months, sometimes a full season — because they depend on soil moisture, temperature, and microbial activity.
segments.tr: どちらもゆっくりと働きます — 数ヶ月、時には丸1シーズンかかることもあります — 土壌の水分、温度、微生物の活動に依存しているからです。

segments.src: One more piece of vocabulary that ties it together: **cation exchange capacity (CEC)**.
segments.tr: それを結びつけるもう一つの語彙：**陽イオン交換容量（CEC）**。

segments.src: Clay and organic matter carry negative charges, and positively charged nutrients — calcium, magnesium, potassium, ammonium — stick to those sites like magnets on a fridge.
segments.tr: 粘土と有機物は負の電荷を帯びており、正に帯電した養分（カルシウム、マグネシウム、カリウム、アンモニウム）は、冷蔵庫の磁石のようにそれらの場所に付着します。

segments.src: High CEC means a soil holds a large nutrient reserve and buffers strongly.
segments.tr: 高いCECは、土壌が大量の養分貯蔵量を保持し、強く緩衝することを示しています。

segments.src: Low CEC (sandy soil) means nutrients leach through fast.
segments.tr: 低いCEC（砂質土壌）は、養分が急速に流亡することを意味します。

segments.src: Same fertilizer, very different behavior.
segments.tr: 同じ肥料でも、挙動は全く異なります。

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: Say you're in Ohio and you plant tomatoes in the same backyard bed for the third summer running.
segments.tr: オハイオ州にいて、3年連続で同じ裏庭の花壇にトマトを植えたとします。

segments.src: You fertilize religiously with a high-nitrogen lawn-style product because it's what's in the garage.
segments.tr: ガレージにあるという理由だけで、高窒素の芝生用製品を熱心に施用します。

segments.src: You get magnificent, dark green, four-foot vines — and almost no fruit.
segments.tr: 見事で濃い緑色の、4フィートのツルが育ちますが — 実はほとんどなりません。

segments.src: That's textbook nutrient imbalance.
segments.tr: それは教科書通りの栄養バランスの崩れです。

segments.src: Excess nitrogen pushes vegetative growth at the expense of flowering and fruit set.
segments.tr: 過剰な窒素は、開花や結実を犠牲にして栄養成長を促進します。

segments.src: Meanwhile, three seasons of removing tomatoes has been quietly withdrawing potassium and phosphorus from the account with no matching deposit.
segments.tr: 一方、トマトを収穫し続けた3シーズンで、見返りの投入がないまま、口座からカリウムとリンが静かに引き出されていました。

segments.src: And in much of the eastern U.S., where rainfall gradually leaches calcium and magnesium out of the topsoil, the pH has been drifting downward year over year — possibly into the mid-5s, where phosphorus availability drops sharply.
segments.tr: そして、降雨によって表土からカルシウムとマグネシウムが徐々に流亡する米国の東部の多くの地域では、pHが年々下降し続けており — おそらく5.5の中頃まで低下し、そこでリンの可給性が急激に低下している可能性があります。

segments.src: The fix costs less than a bag of fertilizer.
segments.tr: 修正にかかる費用は、肥料1袋よりも安価です。

segments.src: Nearly every state has a land-grant university extension service — Ohio State, Penn State, NC State, Texas A&M — running soil testing labs, typically in the $15–$25 range per sample.
segments.tr: ほぼすべての州に、土地交付大学の普及サービス（オハイオ州立大学、ペンシルベニア州立大学、ノースカロライナ州立大学、テキサスA&M大学など）があり、通常1サンプルあたり15ドル〜25ドルの範囲で土壌テストラボを運営しています。

segments.src: You send in a composite of 10–15 cores from around the bed.
segments.tr: 花壇の周囲から10〜15個のコアを採取して混ぜ合わせたものを送ります。

segments.src: What comes back is pH, buffer pH, extractable P and K, calcium, magnesium, organic matter percentage, and CEC, plus a recommendation in pounds per 1,000 square feet.
segments.tr: 返ってくるのは、pH、緩衝pH、抽出可能なPとK、カルシウム、マグネシウム、有機物百分率、CEC、および1,000平方フィートあたりのポンド単位での推奨事項です。

segments.src: If the report says pH 5.4 with a lime requirement of 50 lb per 1,000 sq ft, spreading that lime the previous fall will do more for next year's tomatoes than any amount of fertilizer applied in June.
segments.tr: レポートにpH 5.4、1,000平方フィートあたり50ポンドの石灰要求量と記載されている場合、前年の秋にその石灰を散布することは、6月に施用するいかなる量の肥料よりも、来年のトマトにとって効果的です。

segments.src: You're not adding nutrients — you're unlocking the ones already sitting there.
segments.tr: 新しい養分を追加しているのではなく、すでにそこにあるものを解放しているのです。

segments.src: There's an environmental side too.
segments.tr: 環境面もあります。

segments.src: Nutrients you apply beyond what the crop can use don't vanish.
segments.tr: 作物が利用できる量を超えて施用した養分は消えません。

segments.src: Nitrate leaches into groundwater; phosphorus runs off into surface water and feeds algal blooms.
segments.tr: 硝酸塩は地下水に溶け込み、リンは地表水に流れ出してアオコの発生を促します。

segments.src: The recurring summer blooms in Lake Erie and the hypoxic "dead zone" in the Gulf of Mexico are both driven substantially by nutrient runoff from a very large watershed.
segments.tr: エリー湖で繰り返される夏季のアオコ発生や、メキシコ湾の低酸素の「デッドゾーン」は、どちらも非常に大きな流域からの養分流出によって大幅に引き起こされています。

segments.src: Matching the rate to the actual soil test is the single cheapest thing that helps both your yield and the water downstream.
segments.tr: 実際の土壌テストに合わせて施用量を調整することが、収量と下流の水質の両方を助ける最も安価な単一の方法です。

segments.src: The professional framing for this is the **4Rs**: Right source, Right rate, Right time, Right place.
segments.tr: これに対する専門的な枠組みが**4Rs**です：適切な情報源、適切な施用量、適切な時期、適切な場所。

segments.src: Pick the fertilizer form that fits, apply only what the test calls for, put it down when the crop can use it, and place it where roots will find it.
segments.tr: 適した形態の肥料を選び、テストが要求するものだけを施用し、作物が利用できる時期に施用し、根がそれを見つけられる場所に置きます。

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## 3줄 정리

segments.src: 1. Plants need 17 essential elements; N, P, and K are needed in the largest amounts, which is why every fertilizer bag carries three numbers (`N-P₂O₅-K₂O`) on the front.
segments.tr: 1. 植物には17の必須元素が必要です。N、P、Kは最も多量に必要とされるため、すべての肥料の袋の前面に3つの数字（`N-P₂O₅-K₂O`）が記載されています。

segments.src: 2. Soil pH governs whether nutrients are chemically *available* to roots — phosphorus peaks around pH 6.0–7.0, while iron and zinc become more available as soil turns acidic.
segments.tr: 2. 土壌pHは、養分が根にとって化学的に*利用可能*かどうかを左右します — リンはpH 6.0〜7.0付近でピークを迎え、鉄や亜鉛は土壌が酸性化するにつれてより利用しやすくなります。

segments.src: 3. Buffering capacity, driven by clay and organic matter, resists pH change — so a soil test's buffer pH, not the pH alone, tells you how much lime to apply.
segments.tr: 3. 粘土と有機物によって駆動される緩衝能は、pHの変化に抵抗します — したがって、pH単独ではなく、土壌テストの緩衝pHが、どれだけの石灰を施用すべきかを教えてくれます。

segments.src: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈
segments.tr: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈

segments.src: **Q1.** A 50 lb bag of fertilizer is labeled `10-20-10`.
segments.tr: **Q1.** 50ポンドの肥料の袋に `10-20-10` と表示されています。

segments.src: How many pounds of actual phosphate (P₂O₅) does it contain?
segments.tr: 実際のリン酸（P₂O₅）は何ポンド含まれていますか？

segments.src: - A) 5 lb
segments.tr: - A) 5 lb

segments.src: - B) 10 lb
segments.tr: - B) 10 lb

segments.src: - C) 20 lb
segments.tr: - C) 20 lb

segments.src: - D) 50 lb
segments.tr: - D) 50 lb

segments.src: **Q2.** O/X — Two soils both test at pH 5.5, so they will both need the same amount of lime to reach pH 6.5.
segments.tr: **Q2.** O/X — 2つの土壌のpHがいずれも5.5と測定されたため、pH 6.5に達するにはどちらも同じ量の石灰が必要になります。

segments.src: **Q3.** A gardener's soil has plenty of iron in it, but the plants show yellowing between the leaf veins (chlorosis).
segments.tr: **Q3.** ある庭師の土壌には十分な鉄が含まれていますが、植物の葉脈の間に黄変（クロロシス）が見られます。

segments.src: Which condition is the most likely cause?
segments.tr: 最も可能性の高い原因はどの状態ですか？

segments.src: - A) Soil pH is too low (strongly acidic)
segments.tr: - A) 土壌pHが低すぎる（強い酸性）

segments.src: - B) Soil pH is too high (alkaline)
segments.tr: - B) 土壌pHが高すぎる（アルカリ性）

segments.src: - C) Nitrogen was over-applied
segments.tr: - C) 窒素が過剰に施用された

segments.src: - D) The soil has no cation exchange capacity
segments.tr: - D) 土壌に陽イオン交換容量がない

segments.src: ## 📚 오늘의 용어
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Essential element** — A nutrient a plant cannot complete its life cycle without, and whose role no other element can substitute for; there are 17.
segments.tr: - **必須元素** — 植物がライフサイクルを完了するために不可欠であり、他のどの元素もその役割を代替できない栄養素。17種類あります。

segments.src: - **Macronutrient / Micronutrient** — Classification by the *amount* a plant needs, not by importance; both categories are equally essential.
segments.tr: - **多量栄養素 / 微量栄養素** — 重要性ではなく、植物が必要とする*量*による分類。どちらのカテゴリも同様に必須です。

segments.src: - **Guaranteed analysis (N-P-K)** — The three numbers on a fertilizer label giving percent nitrogen, percent phosphate (P₂O₅), and percent potash (K₂O) by weight.
segments.tr: - **保証成分量（N-P-K）** — 肥料のラベルにある3つの数字で、重量あたりの窒素のパーセント、リン酸（P₂O₅）のパーセント、カリ（K₂O）のパーセントを示します。

segments.src: - **Soil pH** — The acidity or alkalinity of the soil solution on a 0–14 scale; it determines the chemical form, and therefore the availability, of most nutrients.
segments.tr: - **土壌pH** — 0〜14のスケールにおける土壌溶液の酸性度またはアルカリ度。これにより、ほとんどの栄養素の化学的形態、したがって可給性が決定されます。

segments.src: - **Buffering capacity** — A soil's resistance to pH change, supplied by exchangeable acidity held on clay and organic matter; it sets how much lime or sulfur is actually required.
segments.tr: - **緩衝能** — 粘土や有機物に保持された交換可能酸度によって供給される、pH変化に対する土壌の抵抗力。これにより、実際にどれだけの石灰や硫黄が必要かが決まります。

segments.src: - **Cation exchange capacity (CEC)** — The soil's total capacity to hold positively charged nutrients on negatively charged clay and organic matter surfaces; a proxy for nutrient-holding ability.
segments.tr: - **陽イオン交換容量（CEC）** — 負に帯電した粘土および有機物の表面に、正に帯電した栄養素を保持する土壌の総容量。栄養素保持能力の代理指標です。

segments.src: *정답: **Q1 → B (10 lb).** The middle number is percent by weight, so 20% of 50 lb = 10 lb of phosphate.
segments.tr: *正解：**Q1 → B（10 lb）。** 真ん中の数字は重量あたりのパーセントであるため、50 lbの20% = 10 lbのリン酸となります。

segments.src: Note this is P₂O₅, the oxide form used on labels, not elemental phosphorus — elemental P would be about 44% of that figure.*
segments.tr: これはラベルで使用される酸化物の形態であるP₂O₅であり、元素としてのリンではないことに注意してください。元素としてのPはその数値の約44%になります.*

segments.src: ***Q2 → X (False).** Identical pH does not mean identical lime requirement.
segments.tr: ***Q2 → X（偽）。** pHが同じだからといって、必要な石灰の量が同じとは限りません。

segments.src: A heavy clay soil high in organic matter has a large reserve of exchangeable acidity — high buffering — and may need several times the lime a sandy soil needs to make the same pH move.
segments.tr: 有機物が豊富な重い粘土質の土壌は、交換可能酸度の大きな備え（高い緩衝能）を持っており、同じpHの変化を起こすために砂質土壌が必要とする量の数倍の石灰を必要とする場合があります。

segments.src: This is exactly why soil test reports include a buffer pH.*
segments.tr: これこそが、土壌検査レポートに緩衝pHが含まれている理由です.*

segments.src: ***Q3 → B.** Iron becomes progressively less soluble as pH rises; in alkaline soil it precipitates into forms roots cannot absorb.
segments.tr: ***Q3 → B。** pHが上昇するにつれて鉄は次第に溶けにくくなり、アルカリ性土壌では根が吸収できない形態に沈殿します。

segments.src: The plant is iron-deficient despite iron being physically present — a good illustration that total nutrient content and plant-available nutrient content are two different things.
segments.tr: 鉄が物理的に存在しているにもかかわらず植物は鉄欠乏症になっています — これは、総栄養素含有量と植物が利用可能な栄養素含有量がまったく異なる2つのものであることを示す良い例です。

segments.src: Interveinal chlorosis on the youngest leaves is the classic symptom, because iron is not readily remobilized within the plant.*
segments.tr: 一番若い葉の葉脈間クロロシスは典型的な症状です。なぜなら、植物の中で鉄が容易に再移動しないためです。*

de.title: [Agriculture 101 #4] Ihr Boden ist ein Bankkonto — So funktionieren Einzahlungen und Abhebungen

segments.src: > Plants need 17 essential elements, but three of them (N, P, K) do most of the heavy lifting — and soil pH quietly decides how much of any of them a root can actually reach.
segments.tr: > Pflanzen benötigen 17 wesentliche Elemente, aber drei davon (N, P, K) leisten die Hauptarbeit — und der Boden-pH-Wert entscheidet im Stillen darüber, wie viel davon eine Wurzel tatsächlich erreichen kann.

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Think of soil as a checking account that plants draw from every day.
segments.tr: Betrachten Sie den Boden als ein Girokonto, von dem Pflanzen jeden Tag abheben.

segments.src: Plants build themselves out of **essential elements** — nutrients that, if missing, mean the plant literally cannot complete its life cycle.
segments.tr: Pflanzen bauen sich aus **essenziellen Elementen** auf — Nährstoffen, die, wenn sie fehlen, buchstäblich bedeuten, dass die Pflanze ihren Lebenszyklus nicht vollenden kann.

segments.src: There are 17 of them.
segments.tr: Es gibt 17 davon.

segments.src: Three come free from air and water: carbon, hydrogen, oxygen.
segments.tr: Drei kommen kostenlos aus Luft und Wasser: Kohlenstoff, Wasserstoff, Sauerstoff.

segments.src: The other 14 come from the soil.
segments.tr: Die anderen 14 kommen aus dem Boden.

segments.src: Those 14 split into two groups by *quantity needed*, not importance:
segments.tr: Diese 14 unterteilen sich nach *benötigter Menge* in zwei Gruppen, nicht nach Wichtigkeit:

segments.src: - **Macronutrients** (needed in large amounts): nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), plus calcium, magnesium, and sulfur.
segments.tr: - **Makronährstoffe** (in großen Mengen benötigt): Stickstoff (N), Phosphor (P), Kalium (K) sowie Kalzium, Magnesium und Schwefel.

segments.src: - **Micronutrients** (needed in trace amounts): iron, manganese, zinc, copper, boron, molybdenum, chlorine, nickel.
segments.tr: - **Mikronährstoffe** (in Spurenmengen benötigt): Eisen, Mangan, Zink, Kupfer, Bor, Molybdän, Chlor, Nickel.

segments.src: A micronutrient deficiency will kill a crop just as dead as a nitrogen shortage.
segments.tr: Ein Mangel an Mikronährstoffen tötet eine Ernte genauso sicher wie ein Stickstoffmangel.

segments.src: The difference is how much you have to add.
segments.tr: Der Unterschied liegt darin, wie viel man hinzufügen muss.

segments.src: **The Big Three.** Every bag of fertilizer in the U.S.
segments.tr: **Die großen Drei.** Jeder Sack Düngemittel in den USA

segments.src: carries three numbers on the front — say, `10-10-10`.
segments.tr: trägt drei Zahlen auf der Vorderseite — zum Beispiel `10-10-10`.

segments.src: That's the guaranteed analysis: percent nitrogen, percent phosphate (P₂O₅), percent potash (K₂O), by weight.
segments.tr: Das ist die garantierte Analyse: Prozent Stickstoff, Prozent Phosphat (P₂O₅), Prozent Kali (K₂O), nach Gewicht.

segments.src: A 50 lb bag of 10-10-10 contains 5 lb of N, 5 lb of phosphate, and 5 lb of potash.
segments.tr: Ein 50-Pfund-Sack 10-10-10 enthält 5 Pfund N, 5 Pfund Phosphat und 5 Pfund Kali.

segments.src: The rest is carrier and filler.
segments.tr: Der Rest ist Träger- und Füllmaterial.

segments.src: Roughly what each does:
segments.tr: Grob gesagt, was jedes tut:

segments.src: - **Nitrogen** — leaves and stems, chlorophyll, protein. Deficiency shows as pale yellowing on the *oldest* leaves first, because the plant scavenges N from old tissue and moves it to new growth.
segments.tr: - **Stickstoff** — Blätter und Stängel, Chlorophyll, Protein. Ein Mangel zeigt sich als blasse Gelbfärbung zuerst an den *ältesten* Blättern, da die Pflanze N aus altem Gewebe abzieht und zum Neuaustrieb transportiert.

segments.src: - **Phosphorus** — roots, energy transfer, flowering and seed set. Deficiency can show as dull purple-tinged leaves.
segments.tr: - **Phosphor** — Wurzeln, Energietransfer, Blüte und Samenbildung. Ein Mangel kann sich als stumpfe, lila getönte Blätter zeigen.

segments.src: - **Potassium** — water regulation, stomatal control, disease resistance, stalk strength. Deficiency often shows as scorched leaf margins.
segments.tr: - **Kalium** — Wasserregulation, Spaltöffnungssteuerung, Krankheitsresistenz, Stängelfestigkeit. Ein Mangel zeigt sich oft als verbrannte Blattränder.

segments.src: **Now the part most people skip: pH.**
segments.tr: **Jetzt der Teil, den die meisten überspringen: der pH-Wert.**

segments.src: Soil pH is a measure of how acidic or alkaline the soil solution is, on a 0–14 scale where 7 is neutral.
segments.tr: Der Boden-pH-Wert ist ein Maß dafür, wie sauer oder alkalisch die Bodenlösung ist, auf einer Skala von 0 bis 14, wobei 7 neutral ist.

segments.src: It matters because **pH controls nutrient availability**.
segments.tr: Er ist wichtig, weil der **pH-Wert die Nährstoffverfügbarkeit steuert**.

segments.src: You can have plenty of phosphorus in the soil and still starve the crop, because at low pH the phosphorus binds with iron and aluminum into forms roots can't take up.
segments.tr: Man kann reichlich Phosphor im Boden haben und die Kultur trotzdem aushungern lassen, weil sich der Phosphor bei niedrigem pH-Wert mit Eisen und Aluminium zu Formen verbindet, die Wurzeln nicht aufnehmen können.

segments.src: At high pH it binds with calcium instead.
segments.tr: Bei hohem pH-Wert bindet er stattdessen an Kalzium.

segments.src: Phosphorus is most available roughly between pH 6.0 and 7.0 — which is why most field crops and garden vegetables are happiest in the pH 6.0–7.0 window.
segments.tr: Phosphor ist grob zwischen pH 6,0 und 7,0 am besten verfügbar — weshalb die meisten Feldfrüchte und Gemüsegärten im pH-Bereich von 6,0 bis 7,0 am glücklichsten sind.

segments.src: Iron, manganese, and zinc run the opposite way: they get *more* available as soil turns acidic.
segments.tr: Eisen, Mangan und Zink verhalten sich genau umgekehrt: Sie werden *besser* verfügbar, wenn der Boden sauer wird.

segments.src: That's why azaleas and blueberries — acid-lovers — go chlorotic and yellow in alkaline soil.
segments.tr: Deshalb werden Azaleen und Blaubeeren — Säureliebhaber — in alkalischem Boden chlorotisch und gelb.

segments.src: They can't get iron.
segments.tr: Sie bekommen kein Eisen.

segments.src: **Buffering capacity** is why fixing pH is harder than it sounds.
segments.tr: Die **Pufferkapazität** ist der Grund, warum die Korrektur des pH-Werts schwieriger ist, als es klingt.

segments.src: If you add acid to distilled water, the pH plunges.
segments.tr: Wenn man destilliertem Wasser Säure hinzufügt, stürzt der pH-Wert ab.

segments.src: Add the same acid to soil and it barely moves.
segments.tr: Gibt man dieselbe Säure in den Boden, bewegt sich kaum etwas.

segments.src: That resistance is buffering, and it comes from the soil's reserve of exchangeable acidity sitting on clay particles and organic matter — a large hidden pool that keeps refilling the soil solution as you neutralize it.
segments.tr: Dieser Widerstand ist die Pufferung, und er stammt aus der Bodenreserve an austauschbarer Säure, die auf Tonpartikeln und organischer Substanz sitzt — ein großes, verstecktes Reservoir, das die Bodenlösung immer wieder auffüllt, während man sie neutralisiert.

segments.src: Practical consequence: a heavy clay soil rich in organic matter needs *far more* lime to raise its pH one unit than a sandy soil does.
segments.tr: Praktische Konsequenz: Ein schwerer, an organischer Substanzreicher Tonboden benötigt *viel mehr* Kalk, um seinen pH-Wert um eine Einheit anzuheben, als ein Sandboden.

segments.src: That's why a soil test doesn't just report pH — it reports a **buffer pH** or **lime requirement**, which is the number that actually tells you how much lime to spread.
segments.tr: Deshalb meldet ein Bodentest nicht nur den pH-Wert — er meldet einen **Puffer-pH-Wert** oder den **Kalkbedarf**, was die Zahl ist, die tatsächlich angibt, wie viel Kalk gestreut werden muss.

segments.src: Soil test pH   -> where you are now
segments.tr: Soil test pH   -> where you are now

segments.src: Buffer pH      -> how hard it will be to move
segments.tr: Buffer pH      -> how hard it will be to move

segments.src: Lime rate      -> tons per acre to get where you want
segments.tr: Lime rate      -> tons per acre to get where you want

segments.src: The general rules of thumb: **lime** (calcium carbonate) raises pH; **elemental sulfur** lowers it.
segments.tr: Die allgemeinen Daumenregeln: **Kalk** (Kalziumkarbonat) erhöht den pH-Wert; **elementarer Schwefel** senkt ihn.

segments.src: Both work slowly — months, sometimes a full season — because they depend on soil moisture, temperature, and microbial activity.
segments.tr: Beide wirken langsam — Monate, manchmal eine volle Saison — weil sie von Bodenfeuchtigkeit, Temperatur und mikrobieller Aktivität abhängen.

segments.src: One more piece of vocabulary that ties it together: **cation exchange capacity (CEC)**.
segments.tr: Ein weiteres Vokabelstück, das alles zusammenfügt: die **Kationenaustauschkapazität (KAK)**.

segments.src: Clay and organic matter carry negative charges, and positively charged nutrients — calcium, magnesium, potassium, ammonium — stick to those sites like magnets on a fridge.
segments.tr: Ton und organische Substanz tragen negative Ladungen, und positiv geladene Nährstoffe — Kalzium, Magnesium, Kalium, Ammonium — haften an diesen Stellen wie Magnete an einem Kühlschrank.

segments.src: High CEC means a soil holds a large nutrient reserve and buffers strongly.
segments.tr: Eine hohe KAK bedeutet, dass ein Boden eine große Nährstoffreserve hält und stark puffert.

segments.src: Low CEC (sandy soil) means nutrients leach through fast.
segments.tr: Eine niedrige KAK (Sandboden) bedeutet, dass Nährstoffe schnell auswaschen.

segments.src: Same fertilizer, very different behavior.
segments.tr: Gleicher Dünger, sehr unterschiedliches Verhalten.

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: Say you're in Ohio and you plant tomatoes in the same backyard bed for the third summer running.
segments.tr: Angenommen, Sie sind in Ohio und pflanzen im dritten Sommer in Folge Tomaten im selben Beet im Hinterhof an.

segments.src: You fertilize religiously with a high-nitrogen lawn-style product because it's what's in the garage.
segments.tr: Sie düngen gewissenhaft mit einem stickstoffreichen Rasenprodukt, weil das gerade in der Garage steht.

segments.src: You get magnificent, dark green, four-foot vines — and almost no fruit.
segments.tr: Sie erhalten prächtige, dunkelgrüne, 1,20 Meter hohe Ranken — und fast keine Früchte.

segments.src: That's textbook nutrient imbalance.
segments.tr: Das ist Nährstoffunwucht wie aus dem Lehrbuch.

segments.src: Excess nitrogen pushes vegetative growth at the expense of flowering and fruit set.
segments.tr: Überschüssiger Stickstoff treibt das vegetative Wachstum auf Kosten der Blüte und Fruchtbildung voran.

segments.src: Meanwhile, three seasons of removing tomatoes has been quietly withdrawing potassium and phosphorus from the account with no matching deposit.
segments.tr: Unterdessen haben drei Saisons Tomatenentnahme im Stillen Kalium und Phosphor aus dem Konto abgehoben, ohne dass es eine passende Einzahlung gab.

segments.src: And in much of the eastern U.S., where rainfall gradually leaches calcium and magnesium out of the topsoil, the pH has been drifting downward year over year — possibly into the mid-5s, where phosphorus availability drops sharply.
segments.tr: Und in großen Teilen des östlichen US-Raums, wo Niederschläge allmählich Kalzium und Magnesium aus dem Oberboden auswaschen, ist der pH-Wert Jahr für Jahr nach unten gedriftet — möglicherweise in den mittleren 5er-Bereich, wo die Phosphorverfügbarkeit stark abfällt.

segments.src: The fix costs less than a bag of fertilizer.
segments.tr: Die Korrektur kostet weniger als ein Sack Dünger.

segments.src: Nearly every state has a land-grant university extension service — Ohio State, Penn State, NC State, Texas A&M — running soil testing labs, typically in the $15–$25 range per sample.
segments.tr: Fast jeder US-Bundesstaat hat einen land-grant university extension service — Ohio State, Penn State, NC State, Texas A&M —, der Bodenprüflabore betreibt, typischerweise im Bereich von 15 bis 25 US-Dollar pro Probe.

segments.src: You send in a composite of 10–15 cores from around the bed.
segments.tr: Sie schicken eine Mischprobe aus 10 bis 15 Bohrkernen aus dem gesamten Beet ein.

segments.src: What comes back is pH, buffer pH, extractable P and K, calcium, magnesium, organic matter percentage, and CEC, plus a recommendation in pounds per 1,000 square feet.
segments.tr: Zurück kommen pH-Wert, Puffer-pH, extrahierbares P und K, Kalzium, Magnesium, der Prozentsatz an organischer Substanz und die KAK sowie eine Empfehlung in Pfund pro 1.000 Quadratfuß.

segments.src: If the report says pH 5.4 with a lime requirement of 50 lb per 1,000 sq ft, spreading that lime the previous fall will do more for next year's tomatoes than any amount of fertilizer applied in June.
segments.tr: Wenn der Bericht einen pH-Wert von 5,4 mit einem Kalkbedarf von 50 Pfund pro 1.000 sq ft ausweist, wird das Ausbringen dieses Kalks im vorherigen Herbst mehr für die Tomaten des nächsten Jahres tun als jede im Juni ausgebrachte Düngermenge.

segments.src: You're not adding nutrients — you're unlocking the ones already sitting there.
segments.tr: Sie fügen keine Nährstoffe hinzu — Sie schalten die frei, die bereits dort sitzen.

segments.src: There's an environmental side too.
segments.tr: Es gibt auch eine ökologische Seite.

segments.src: Nutrients you apply beyond what the crop can use don't vanish.
segments.tr: Nährstoffe, die Sie über das hinaus ausbringen, was die Kultur nutzen kann, verschwinden nicht.

segments.src: Nitrate leaches into groundwater; phosphorus runs off into surface water and feeds algal blooms.
segments.tr: Nitrat wäscht ins Grundwasser aus; Phosphor schwemmt in Oberflächengewässer und nährt Algenblüten.

segments.src: The recurring summer blooms in Lake Erie and the hypoxic "dead zone" in the Gulf of Mexico are both driven substantially by nutrient runoff from a very large watershed.
segments.tr: Die wiederkehrenden Sommerblüten im Eriesee und die hypoxische "Todeszone" im Golf von Mexiko werden beide maßgeblich durch Nährstoffabflüsse aus einem sehr großen Einzugsgebiet angetrieben.

segments.src: Matching the rate to the actual soil test is the single cheapest thing that helps both your yield and the water downstream.
segments.tr: Die Anpassung der Aufwandmenge an den tatsächlichen Bodentest ist das mit Abstand günstigste Mittel, das sowohl Ihrem Ertrag als auch dem Wasser stromabwärts zugutekommt.

segments.src: The professional framing for this is the **4Rs**: Right source, Right rate, Right time, Right place.
segments.tr: Der professionelle Rahmen dafür sind die **4Rs**: Richtige Quelle, Richtige Menge, Richtige Zeit, Richtiger Ort.

segments.src: Pick the fertilizer form that fits, apply only what the test calls for, put it down when the crop can use it, and place it where roots will find it.
segments.tr: Wählen Sie die Düngerform, die passt, bringen Sie nur aus, was der Test verlangt, bringen Sie ihn aus, wenn die Kultur ihn nutzen kann, und platzieren Sie ihn dort, wo Wurzeln ihn finden werden.

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## 3줄 정리

segments.src: 1. Plants need 17 essential elements; N, P, and K are needed in the largest amounts, which is why every fertilizer bag carries three numbers (`N-P₂O₅-K₂O`) on the front.
segments.tr: 1. Pflanzen benötigen 17 essenzielle Elemente; N, P und K werden in den größten Mengen benötigt, weshalb jeder Düngersack drei Zahlen (`N-P₂O₅-K₂O`) auf der Vorderseite trägt.

segments.src: 2. Soil pH governs whether nutrients are chemically *available* to roots — phosphorus peaks around pH 6.0–7.0, while iron and zinc become more available as soil turns acidic.
segments.tr: 2. Der Boden-pH-Wert regelt, ob Nährstoffe für Wurzeln chemisch *verfügbar* sind — Phosphor hat sein Maximum bei etwa pH 6,0–7,0, während Eisen und Zink verfügbarer werden, wenn der Boden sauer wird.

segments.src: 3. Buffering capacity, driven by clay and organic matter, resists pH change — so a soil test's buffer pH, not the pH alone, tells you how much lime to apply.
segments.tr: 3. Die Pufferkapazität, angetrieben durch Ton und organische Substanz, widersetzt sich pH-Änderungen — daher sagt Ihnen der Puffer-pH-Wert eines Bodentests, nicht der pH-Wert allein, wie viel Kalk ausgebracht werden muss.

segments.src: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈
segments.tr: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈

segments.src: **Q1.** A 50 lb bag of fertilizer is labeled `10-20-10`.
segments.tr: **F1.** Ein 50-Pfund-Sack Dünger ist mit `10-20-10` beschriftet.

segments.src: How many pounds of actual phosphate (P₂O₅) does it contain?
segments.tr: Wie viele Pfund echtes Phosphat (P₂O₅) enthält er?

segments.src: - A) 5 lb
segments.tr: - A) 5 Pfund

segments.src: - B) 10 lb
segments.tr: - B) 10 Pfund

segments.src: - C) 20 lb
segments.tr: - C) 20 Pfund

segments.src: - D) 50 lb
segments.tr: - D) 50 Pfund

segments.src: **Q2.** O/X — Two soils both test at pH 5.5, so they will both need the same amount of lime to reach pH 6.5.
segments.tr: **F2.** R/F — Zwei Böden haben beide einen Testwert von pH 5,5, daher benötigen sie beide dieselbe Menge Kalk, um pH 6,5 zu erreichen.

segments.src: **Q3.** A gardener's soil has plenty of iron in it, but the plants show yellowing between the leaf veins (chlorosis).
segments.tr: **F3.** Der Boden eines Gärtners enthält reichlich Eisen, aber die Pflanzen zeigen eine Gelbfärbung zwischen den Blattadern (Chlorose).

segments.src: Which condition is the most likely cause?
segments.tr: Welcher Zustand ist die wahrscheinlichste Ursache?

segments.src: - A) Soil pH is too low (strongly acidic)
segments.tr: - A) Der Boden-pH-Wert ist zu niedrig (stark sauer)

segments.src: - B) Soil pH is too high (alkaline)
segments.tr: - B) Der Boden-pH-Wert ist zu hoch (alkalisch)

segments.src: - C) Nitrogen was over-applied
segments.tr: - C) Stickstoff wurde übermäßig ausgebracht

segments.src: - D) The soil has no cation exchange capacity
segments.tr: - D) Der Boden hat keine Kationenaustauschkapazität

segments.src: ## 📚 오늘의 용어
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Essential element** — A nutrient a plant cannot complete its life cycle without, and whose role no other element can substitute for; there are 17.
segments.tr: - **Essenzielles Element** — Ein Nährstoff, ohne den eine Pflanze ihren Lebenszyklus nicht vollenden kann und dessen Rolle kein anderes Element ersetzen kann; es gibt 17.

segments.src: - **Macronutrient / Micronutrient** — Classification by the *amount* a plant needs, not by importance; both categories are equally essential.
segments.tr: - **Makronährstoff / Mikronährstoff** — Klassifizierung nach der *Menge*, die eine Pflanze benötigt, nicht nach Wichtigkeit; beide Kategorien sind gleichermaßen essenziell.

segments.src: - **Guaranteed analysis (N-P-K)** — The three numbers on a fertilizer label giving percent nitrogen, percent phosphate (P₂O₅), and percent potash (K₂O) by weight.
segments.tr: - **Garantierte Analyse (N-P-K)** — Die drei Zahlen auf einem Düngersetikett, die den Prozentsatz an Stickstoff, Phosphat (P₂O₅) und Kali (K₂O) nach Gewicht angeben.

segments.src: - **Soil pH** — The acidity or alkalinity of the soil solution on a 0–14 scale; it determines the chemical form, and therefore the availability, of most nutrients.
segments.tr: - **Boden-pH-Wert** — Die Säure oder Alkalinität der Bodenlösung auf einer Skala von 0 bis 14; sie bestimmt die chemische Form und damit die Verfügbarkeit der meisten Nährstoffe.

segments.src: - **Buffering capacity** — A soil's resistance to pH change, supplied by exchangeable acidity held on clay and organic matter; it sets how much lime or sulfur is actually required.
segments.tr: - **Pufferkapazität** — Der Widerstand eines Bodens gegen pH-Änderungen, bereitgestellt durch austauschbare Säure, die an Ton und organischer Substanz gebunden ist; sie legt fest, wie viel Kalk oder Schwefel tatsächlich erforderlich ist.

segments.src: - **Cation exchange capacity (CEC)** — The soil's total capacity to hold positively charged nutrients on negatively charged clay and organic matter surfaces; a proxy for nutrient-holding ability.
segments.tr: - **Kationenaustauschkapazität (KAK)** — Die Gesamtkapazität des Bodens, positiv geladene Nährstoffe an negativ geladenen Ton- und organischen Substanzoberflächen zu halten; ein Indikator für die Nährstoffhaltefähigkeit.

segments.src: *정답: **Q1 → B (10 lb).** The middle number is percent by weight, so 20% of 50 lb = 10 lb of phosphate.
segments.tr: *Antworten: **F1 → B (10 Pfund).** Die mittlere Zahl ist der Prozentsatz nach Gewicht, also sind 20% von 50 Pfund = 10 Pfund Phosphat.

segments.src: Note this is P₂O₅, the oxide form used on labels, not elemental phosphorus — elemental P would be about 44% of that figure.*
segments.tr: Beachten Sie, dass dies P₂O₅ ist, die auf Etiketten verwendete Oxidform, nicht elementarer Phosphor — elementares P würde etwa 44% dieser Zahl ausmachen.*

segments.src: ***Q2 → X (False).** Identical pH does not mean identical lime requirement.
segments.tr: ***F2 → F (Falsch).** Ein identischer pH-Wert bedeutet keinen identischen Kalkbedarf.

segments.src: A heavy clay soil high in organic matter has a large reserve of exchangeable acidity — high buffering — and may need several times the lime a sandy soil needs to make the same pH move.
segments.tr: Ein schwerer Tonboden mit viel organischer Substanz hat eine große Reserve an austauschbarer Säure — hohe Pufferung — und benötigt möglicherweise ein Vielfaches des Kalks, den ein Sandboden benötigt, um denselben pH-Sprung zu machen.

segments.src: This is exactly why soil test reports include a buffer pH.*
segments.tr: Genau deshalb enthalten Bodentestberichte einen Puffer-pH-Wert.*

segments.src: ***Q3 → B.** Iron becomes progressively less soluble as pH rises; in alkaline soil it precipitates into forms roots cannot absorb.
segments.tr: ***F3 → B.** Eisen wird mit steigendem pH-Wert zunehmend unlöslicher; in alkalischem Boden fällt es in Formen aus, die Wurzeln nicht absorbieren können.

segments.src: The plant is iron-deficient despite iron being physically present — a good illustration that total nutrient content and plant-available nutrient content are two different things.
segments.tr: Die Pflanze ist eisenarm, obwohl Eisen physisch vorhanden ist — ein gutes Beispiel dafür, dass der Gesamtnährstoffgehalt und der pflanzenverfügbare Nährstoffgehalt zwei verschiedene Dinge sind.

segments.src: Interveinal chlorosis on the youngest leaves is the classic symptom, because iron is not readily remobilized within the plant.*
segments.tr: Intervenale Chlorose an den jüngsten Blättern ist das klassische Symptom, da Eisen in der Pflanze nicht leicht remobilisiert wird.*

vi.title: [Nông nghiệp 101 #4] Đất của bạn là một tài khoản ngân hàng — Đây là cách thức hoạt động của việc gửi và rút tiền

segments.src: > Plants need 17 essential elements, but three of them (N, P, K) do most of the heavy lifting — and soil pH quietly decides how much of any of them a root can actually reach.
segments.tr: > Thực vật cần 17 nguyên tố thiết yếu, nhưng ba trong số đó (N, P, K) đảm nhận phần lớn công việc nặng nhọc — và độ pH của đất âm thầm quyết định lượng dinh dưỡng mà rễ cây thực sự có thể tiếp cận.

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## Khái niệm hôm nay

segments.src: Think of soil as a checking account that plants draw from every day.
segments.tr: Hãy coi đất như một tài khoản thanh toán mà thực vật rút ra mỗi ngày.

segments.src: Plants build themselves out of **essential elements** — nutrients that, if missing, mean the plant literally cannot complete its life cycle.
segments.tr: Thực vật tự xây dựng cơ thể từ các **nguyên tố thiết yếu** — những chất dinh dưỡng mà nếu thiếu chúng, thực vật thực sự không thể hoàn thành vòng đời của mình.

segments.src: There are 17 of them.
segments.tr: Có 17 nguyên tố như vậy.

segments.src: Three come free from air and water: carbon, hydrogen, oxygen.
segments.tr: Ba nguyên tố đến miễn phí từ không khí và nước: carbon, hydro, oxy.

segments.src: The other 14 come from the soil.
segments.tr: 14 nguyên tố còn lại đến từ đất.

segments.src: Those 14 split into two groups by *quantity needed*, not importance:
segments.tr: 14 nguyên tố đó được chia thành hai nhóm dựa trên *số lượng cần thiết*, không phải tầm quan trọng:

segments.src: - **Macronutrients** (needed in large amounts): nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), plus calcium, magnesium, and sulfur.
segments.tr: - **Đa lượng** (cần với số lượng lớn): nitơ (N), phốt pho (P), kali (K), cộng với canxi, magiê và lưu huỳnh.

segments.src: - **Micronutrients** (needed in trace amounts): iron, manganese, zinc, copper, boron, molybdenum, chlorine, nickel.
segments.tr: - **Vi lượng** (cần với số lượng vết): sắt, mangan, kẽm, đồng, bo, molypden, clo, niken.

segments.src: A micronutrient deficiency will kill a crop just as dead as a nitrogen shortage.
segments.tr: Sự thiếu hụt vi lượng sẽ làm chết cây trồng giống như sự thiếu hụt nitơ.

segments.src: The difference is how much you have to add.
segments.tr: Sự khác biệt nằm ở lượng bạn cần bổ sung.

segments.src: **The Big Three.** Every bag of fertilizer in the U.S.
segments.tr: **Bộ ba quan trọng.** Mỗi bao phân bón ở Hoa Kỳ

segments.src: carries three numbers on the front — say, `10-10-10`.
segments.tr: đều có ba con số ở mặt trước — ví dụ, `10-10-10`.

segments.src: That's the guaranteed analysis: percent nitrogen, percent phosphate (P₂O₅), percent potash (K₂O), by weight.
segments.tr: Đó là phân tích đảm bảo: phần trăm nitơ, phần trăm phốt phát (P₂O₅), phần trăm kali (K₂O), tính theo trọng lượng.

segments.src: A 50 lb bag of 10-10-10 contains 5 lb of N, 5 lb of phosphate, and 5 lb of potash.
segments.tr: Một bao 50 lb loại 10-10-10 chứa 5 lb N, 5 lb phốt phát và 5 lb kali.

segments.src: The rest is carrier and filler.
segments.tr: Phần còn lại là chất mang và chất độn.

segments.src: Roughly what each does:
segments.tr: Tóm tắt công dụng của từng loại:

segments.src: - **Nitrogen** — leaves and stems, chlorophyll, protein. Deficiency shows as pale yellowing on the *oldest* leaves first, because the plant scavenges N from old tissue and moves it to new growth.
segments.tr: - **Nitơ** — lá và thân, diệp lục, protein. Sự thiếu hụt biểu hiện bằng hiện tượng vàng nhạt trên các lá *già nhất* trước tiên, vì cây lấy N từ mô cũ và chuyển đến phần tăng trưởng mới.

segments.src: - **Phosphorus** — roots, energy transfer, flowering and seed set. Deficiency can show as dull purple-tinged leaves.
segments.tr: - **Phốt pho** — rễ, chuyển hóa năng lượng, ra hoa và kết hạt. Sự thiếu hụt có thể biểu hiện bằng lá có màu tím xỉn.

segments.src: - **Potassium** — water regulation, stomatal control, disease resistance, stalk strength. Deficiency often shows as scorched leaf margins.
segments.tr: - **Kali** — điều hòa nước, kiểm soát khí khổng, kháng bệnh, độ cứng của thân. Sự thiếu hụt thường biểu hiện bằng mép lá bị cháy.

segments.src: **Now the part most people skip: pH.**
segments.tr: **Bây giờ là phần mà hầu hết mọi người bỏ qua: pH.**

segments.src: Soil pH is a measure of how acidic or alkaline the soil solution is, on a 0–14 scale where 7 is neutral.
segments.tr: Độ pH của đất là thước đo mức độ axit hoặc kiềm của dung dịch đất, trên thang đo 0–14, trong đó 7 là trung tính.

segments.src: It matters because **pH controls nutrient availability**.
segments.tr: Điều này quan trọng vì **pH kiểm soát khả năng cung cấp dinh dưỡng**.

segments.src: You can have plenty of phosphorus in the soil and still starve the crop, because at low pH the phosphorus binds with iron and aluminum into forms roots can't take up.
segments.tr: Bạn có thể có rất nhiều phốt pho trong đất nhưng cây trồng vẫn bị đói, vì ở độ pH thấp, phốt pho liên kết với sắt và nhôm thành các dạng mà rễ không thể hấp thụ.

segments.src: At high pH it binds with calcium instead.
segments.tr: Ở độ pH cao, nó lại liên kết với canxi.

segments.src: Phosphorus is most available roughly between pH 6.0 and 7.0 — which is why most field crops and garden vegetables are happiest in the pH 6.0–7.0 window.
segments.tr: Phốt pho khả dụng nhất ở khoảng pH 6.0 đến 7.0 — đó là lý do tại sao hầu hết các loại cây trồng trên đồng ruộng và rau vườn phát triển tốt nhất trong khoảng pH 6.0–7.0.

segments.src: Iron, manganese, and zinc run the opposite way: they get *more* available as soil turns acidic.
segments.tr: Sắt, mangan và kẽm lại theo chiều ngược lại: chúng trở nên *khả dụng hơn* khi đất trở nên axit.

segments.src: That's why azaleas and blueberries — acid-lovers — go chlorotic and yellow in alkaline soil.
segments.tr: Đó là lý do tại sao hoa đỗ quyên và việt quất — những loài ưa axit — bị úa vàng trong đất kiềm.

segments.src: They can't get iron.
segments.tr: Chúng không thể hấp thụ sắt.

segments.src: **Buffering capacity** is why fixing pH is harder than it sounds.
segments.tr: **Khả năng đệm** là lý do tại sao việc điều chỉnh pH khó hơn vẻ ngoài của nó.

segments.src: If you add acid to distilled water, the pH plunges.
segments.tr: Nếu bạn thêm axit vào nước cất, độ pH sẽ giảm mạnh.

segments.src: Add the same acid to soil and it barely moves.
segments.tr: Thêm cùng lượng axit đó vào đất thì độ pH hầu như không thay đổi.

segments.src: That resistance is buffering, and it comes from the soil's reserve of exchangeable acidity sitting on clay particles and organic matter — a large hidden pool that keeps refilling the soil solution as you neutralize it.
segments.tr: Sự kháng cự đó chính là khả năng đệm, và nó đến từ nguồn dự trữ axit trao đổi của đất nằm trên các hạt sét và chất hữu cơ — một bể chứa ẩn lớn liên tục bổ sung vào dung dịch đất khi bạn trung hòa nó.

segments.src: Practical consequence: a heavy clay soil rich in organic matter needs *far more* lime to raise its pH one unit than a sandy soil does.
segments.tr: Hệ quả thực tế: đất sét nặng giàu chất hữu cơ cần *nhiều vôi hơn hẳn* để tăng độ pH lên một đơn vị so với đất cát.

segments.src: That's why a soil test doesn't just report pH — it reports a **buffer pH** or **lime requirement**, which is the number that actually tells you how much lime to spread.
segments.tr: Đó là lý do tại sao xét nghiệm đất không chỉ báo cáo độ pH — nó còn báo cáo **pH đệm** hoặc **nhu cầu vôi**, đây là con số thực sự cho bạn biết cần rải bao nhiêu vôi.

segments.src: Soil test pH   -> where you are now
segments.tr: Soil test pH   -> where you are now

segments.src: Buffer pH      -> how hard it will be to move
segments.tr: Buffer pH      -> how hard it will be to move

segments.src: Lime rate      -> tons per acre to get where you want
segments.tr: Lime rate      -> tons per acre to get where you want

segments.src: The general rules of thumb: **lime** (calcium carbonate) raises pH; **elemental sulfur** lowers it.
segments.tr: Các quy tắc chung: **vôi** (canxi cacbonat) làm tăng độ pH; **lưu huỳnh nguyên tố** làm giảm độ pH.

segments.src: Both work slowly — months, sometimes a full season — because they depend on soil moisture, temperature, and microbial activity.
segments.tr: Cả hai đều hoạt động chậm — mất nhiều tháng, đôi khi cả một mùa — vì chúng phụ thuộc vào độ ẩm của đất, nhiệt độ và hoạt động của vi sinh vật.

segments.src: One more piece of vocabulary that ties it together: **cation exchange capacity (CEC)**.
segments.tr: Thêm một thuật ngữ nữa kết nối mọi thứ: **khả năng trao đổi cation (CEC)**.

segments.src: Clay and organic matter carry negative charges, and positively charged nutrients — calcium, magnesium, potassium, ammonium — stick to those sites like magnets on a fridge.
segments.tr: Đất sét và chất hữu cơ mang điện tích âm, và các chất dinh dưỡng mang điện tích dương — canxi, magiê, kali, amoni — bám vào các vị trí đó như nam châm trên tủ lạnh.

segments.src: High CEC means a soil holds a large nutrient reserve and buffers strongly.
segments.tr: CEC cao có nghĩa là đất giữ được nguồn dự trữ dinh dưỡng lớn và có khả năng đệm mạnh.

segments.src: Low CEC (sandy soil) means nutrients leach through fast.
segments.tr: CEC thấp (đất cát) có nghĩa là chất dinh dưỡng bị rửa trôi nhanh chóng.

segments.src: Same fertilizer, very different behavior.
segments.tr: Cùng một loại phân bón, nhưng hiệu quả rất khác nhau.

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## Trong cuộc sống hàng ngày

segments.src: Say you're in Ohio and you plant tomatoes in the same backyard bed for the third summer running.
segments.tr: Giả sử bạn ở Ohio và bạn trồng cà chua trong cùng một luống đất ở sân sau trong mùa hè thứ ba liên tiếp.

segments.src: You fertilize religiously with a high-nitrogen lawn-style product because it's what's in the garage.
segments.tr: Bạn bón phân đều đặn bằng một loại sản phẩm dành cho bãi cỏ có hàm lượng nitơ cao vì đó là thứ có sẵn trong nhà để xe.

segments.src: You get magnificent, dark green, four-foot vines — and almost no fruit.
segments.tr: Bạn có những cây cà chua xanh tốt, cao bốn feet — nhưng hầu như không có quả.

segments.src: That's textbook nutrient imbalance.
segments.tr: Đó là sự mất cân bằng dinh dưỡng điển hình trong sách giáo khoa.

segments.src: Excess nitrogen pushes vegetative growth at the expense of flowering and fruit set.
segments.tr: Nitơ dư thừa thúc đẩy sự phát triển sinh dưỡng nhưng lại làm giảm khả năng ra hoa và đậu quả.

segments.src: Meanwhile, three seasons of removing tomatoes has been quietly withdrawing potassium and phosphorus from the account with no matching deposit.
segments.tr: Trong khi đó, ba mùa thu hoạch cà chua đã âm thầm rút kali và phốt pho khỏi tài khoản mà không có khoản gửi bù đắp tương ứng.

segments.src: And in much of the eastern U.S., where rainfall gradually leaches calcium and magnesium out of the topsoil, the pH has been drifting downward year over year — possibly into the mid-5s, where phosphorus availability drops sharply.
segments.tr: Và ở phần lớn miền đông Hoa Kỳ, nơi lượng mưa dần rửa trôi canxi và magiê khỏi lớp đất mặt, độ pH đã giảm dần qua từng năm — có thể xuống mức 5,5, nơi khả năng cung cấp phốt pho giảm mạnh.

segments.src: The fix costs less than a bag of fertilizer.
segments.tr: Cách khắc phục tốn ít chi phí hơn một bao phân bón.

segments.src: Nearly every state has a land-grant university extension service — Ohio State, Penn State, NC State, Texas A&M — running soil testing labs, typically in the $15–$25 range per sample.
segments.tr: Hầu như mọi tiểu bang đều có dịch vụ khuyến nông của các trường đại học công lập — Ohio State, Penn State, NC State, Texas A&M — vận hành các phòng thí nghiệm xét nghiệm đất, thường có giá từ $15–$25 mỗi mẫu.

segments.src: You send in a composite of 10–15 cores from around the bed.
segments.tr: Bạn gửi một mẫu hỗn hợp gồm 10–15 lõi đất từ xung quanh luống.

segments.src: What comes back is pH, buffer pH, extractable P and K, calcium, magnesium, organic matter percentage, and CEC, plus a recommendation in pounds per 1,000 square feet.
segments.tr: Kết quả trả về là pH, pH đệm, P và K có thể chiết xuất, canxi, magiê, tỷ lệ phần trăm chất hữu cơ và CEC, cộng với khuyến nghị tính bằng pound trên 1.000 feet vuông.

segments.src: If the report says pH 5.4 with a lime requirement of 50 lb per 1,000 sq ft, spreading that lime the previous fall will do more for next year's tomatoes than any amount of fertilizer applied in June.
segments.tr: Nếu báo cáo cho biết pH 5.4 với nhu cầu vôi là 50 lb trên 1.000 sq ft, việc rải vôi đó vào mùa thu trước sẽ có lợi cho cà chua năm sau hơn bất kỳ lượng phân bón nào được bón vào tháng Sáu.

segments.src: You're not adding nutrients — you're unlocking the ones already sitting there.
segments.tr: Bạn không phải đang thêm chất dinh dưỡng — bạn đang giải phóng những chất đã có sẵn ở đó.

segments.src: There's an environmental side too.
segments.tr: Ngoài ra còn có khía cạnh môi trường.

segments.src: Nutrients you apply beyond what the crop can use don't vanish.
segments.tr: Các chất dinh dưỡng bạn bón vượt quá mức cây trồng có thể sử dụng sẽ không biến mất.

segments.src: Nitrate leaches into groundwater; phosphorus runs off into surface water and feeds algal blooms.
segments.tr: Nitrat rửa trôi vào nước ngầm; phốt pho chảy tràn vào nước mặt và nuôi dưỡng tảo nở hoa.

segments.src: The recurring summer blooms in Lake Erie and the hypoxic "dead zone" in the Gulf of Mexico are both driven substantially by nutrient runoff from a very large watershed.
segments.tr: Hiện tượng tảo nở hoa tái diễn vào mùa hè ở Hồ Erie và "vùng chết" thiếu oxy ở Vịnh Mexico đều bị thúc đẩy đáng kể bởi dòng chảy dinh dưỡng từ một lưu vực rất lớn.

segments.src: Matching the rate to the actual soil test is the single cheapest thing that helps both your yield and the water downstream.
segments.tr: Điều chỉnh tỷ lệ bón theo kết quả xét nghiệm đất thực tế là cách rẻ nhất giúp ích cho cả năng suất của bạn và nguồn nước ở hạ lưu.

segments.src: The professional framing for this is the **4Rs**: Right source, Right rate, Right time, Right place.
segments.tr: Cách tiếp cận chuyên nghiệp cho việc này là **4R**: Đúng nguồn, Đúng tỷ lệ, Đúng thời điểm, Đúng vị trí.

segments.src: Pick the fertilizer form that fits, apply only what the test calls for, put it down when the crop can use it, and place it where roots will find it.
segments.tr: Chọn loại phân bón phù hợp, chỉ bón theo yêu cầu của xét nghiệm, bón khi cây trồng có thể sử dụng và đặt ở nơi rễ cây có thể tìm thấy.

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## Tóm tắt 3 ý chính

segments.src: 1. Plants need 17 essential elements; N, P, and K are needed in the largest amounts, which is why every fertilizer bag carries three numbers (`N-P₂O₅-K₂O`) on the front.
segments.tr: 1. Thực vật cần 17 nguyên tố thiết yếu; N, P và K là những nguyên tố cần với số lượng lớn nhất, đó là lý do tại sao mọi bao phân bón đều có ba con số (`N-P₂O₅-K₂O`) ở mặt trước.

segments.src: 2. Soil pH governs whether nutrients are chemically *available* to roots — phosphorus peaks around pH 6.0–7.0, while iron and zinc become more available as soil turns acidic.
segments.tr: 2. Độ pH của đất quyết định liệu các chất dinh dưỡng có *khả dụng* về mặt hóa học đối với rễ cây hay không — phốt pho đạt đỉnh ở khoảng pH 6.0–7.0, trong khi sắt và kẽm trở nên khả dụng hơn khi đất trở nên axit.

segments.src: 3. Buffering capacity, driven by clay and organic matter, resists pH change — so a soil test's buffer pH, not the pH alone, tells you how much lime to apply.
segments.tr: 3. Khả năng đệm, được tạo ra bởi đất sét và chất hữu cơ, chống lại sự thay đổi pH — vì vậy pH đệm của xét nghiệm đất, chứ không phải chỉ riêng độ pH, mới cho bạn biết cần bón bao nhiêu vôi.

segments.tr: ## ✅ Tự kiểm tra

segments.src: **Q1.** A 50 lb bag of fertilizer is labeled `10-20-10`.
segments.tr: **Q1.** Một bao phân bón 50 lb được dán nhãn `10-20-10`.

segments.src: How many pounds of actual phosphate (P₂O₅) does it contain?
segments.tr: Nó chứa bao nhiêu pound phốt phát (P₂O₅) thực tế?

segments.src: - A) 5 lb
segments.tr: - A) 5 lb

segments.src: - B) 10 lb
segments.tr: - B) 10 lb

segments.src: - C) 20 lb
segments.tr: - C) 20 lb

segments.src: - D) 50 lb
segments.tr: - D) 50 lb

segments.src: **Q2.** O/X — Two soils both test at pH 5.5, so they will both need the same amount of lime to reach pH 6.5.
segments.tr: **Q2.** Đúng/Sai — Hai loại đất đều có kết quả xét nghiệm pH 5.5, vì vậy cả hai sẽ cần cùng một lượng vôi để đạt pH 6.5.

segments.src: **Q3.** A gardener's soil has plenty of iron in it, but the plants show yellowing between the leaf veins (chlorosis).
segments.tr: **Q3.** Đất của một người làm vườn có rất nhiều sắt, nhưng cây trồng lại bị vàng giữa các gân lá (bệnh úa vàng).

segments.src: Which condition is the most likely cause?
segments.tr: Điều kiện nào là nguyên nhân có khả năng nhất?

segments.src: - A) Soil pH is too low (strongly acidic)
segments.tr: - A) Độ pH của đất quá thấp (axit mạnh)

segments.src: - B) Soil pH is too high (alkaline)
segments.tr: - B) Độ pH của đất quá cao (kiềm)

segments.src: - C) Nitrogen was over-applied
segments.tr: - C) Bón quá nhiều nitơ

segments.src: - D) The soil has no cation exchange capacity
segments.tr: - D) Đất không có khả năng trao đổi cation

segments.src: ## 📚 오늘의 용어
segments.tr: ## 📚 Thuật ngữ hôm nay

segments.src: - **Essential element** — A nutrient a plant cannot complete its life cycle without, and whose role no other element can substitute for; there are 17.
segments.tr: - **Nguyên tố thiết yếu** — Một chất dinh dưỡng mà thực vật không thể hoàn thành vòng đời nếu thiếu nó, và vai trò của nó không nguyên tố nào khác có thể thay thế; có 17 nguyên tố.

segments.src: - **Macronutrient / Micronutrient** — Classification by the *amount* a plant needs, not by importance; both categories are equally essential.
segments.tr: - **Đa lượng / Vi lượng** — Phân loại theo *số lượng* mà thực vật cần, không phải theo tầm quan trọng; cả hai loại đều thiết yếu như nhau.

segments.src: - **Guaranteed analysis (N-P-K)** — The three numbers on a fertilizer label giving percent nitrogen, percent phosphate (P₂O₅), and percent potash (K₂O) by weight.
segments.tr: - **Phân tích đảm bảo (N-P-K)** — Ba con số trên nhãn phân bón cho biết phần trăm nitơ, phần trăm phốt phát (P₂O₅) và phần trăm kali (K₂O) theo trọng lượng.

segments.src: - **Soil pH** — The acidity or alkalinity of the soil solution on a 0–14 scale; it determines the chemical form, and therefore the availability, of most nutrients.
segments.tr: - **Độ pH của đất** — Độ axit hoặc kiềm của dung dịch đất trên thang đo 0–14; nó xác định dạng hóa học, và do đó là khả năng cung cấp, của hầu hết các chất dinh dưỡng.

segments.src: - **Buffering capacity** — A soil's resistance to pH change, supplied by exchangeable acidity held on clay and organic matter; it sets how much lime or sulfur is actually required.
segments.tr: - **Khả năng đệm** — Khả năng chống lại sự thay đổi pH của đất, được cung cấp bởi axit trao đổi giữ trên đất sét và chất hữu cơ; nó quyết định lượng vôi hoặc lưu huỳnh thực sự cần thiết.

segments.src: - **Cation exchange capacity (CEC)** — The soil's total capacity to hold positively charged nutrients on negatively charged clay and organic matter surfaces; a proxy for nutrient-holding ability.
segments.tr: - **Khả năng trao đổi cation (CEC)** — Tổng khả năng của đất trong việc giữ các chất dinh dưỡng mang điện tích dương trên bề mặt đất sét và chất hữu cơ mang điện tích âm; một chỉ số đại diện cho khả năng giữ dinh dưỡng.

segments.src: *정답: **Q1 → B (10 lb).** The middle number is percent by weight, so 20% of 50 lb = 10 lb of phosphate.
segments.tr: *Đáp án: **Q1 → B (10 lb).** Con số ở giữa là phần trăm theo trọng lượng, vì vậy 20% của 50 lb = 10 lb phốt phát.

segments.src: Note this is P₂O₅, the oxide form used on labels, not elemental phosphorus — elemental P would be about 44% of that figure.*
segments.tr: Lưu ý đây là P₂O₅, dạng oxit được sử dụng trên nhãn, không phải phốt pho nguyên tố — phốt pho nguyên tố sẽ bằng khoảng 44% con số đó.*

segments.src: ***Q2 → X (False).** Identical pH does not mean identical lime requirement.
segments.tr: ***Q2 → X (Sai).** Độ pH giống nhau không có nghĩa là nhu cầu vôi giống nhau.

segments.src: A heavy clay soil high in organic matter has a large reserve of exchangeable acidity — high buffering — and may need several times the lime a sandy soil needs to make the same pH move.
segments.tr: Đất sét nặng giàu chất hữu cơ có nguồn dự trữ axit trao đổi lớn — khả năng đệm cao — và có thể cần lượng vôi gấp nhiều lần so với đất cát để tạo ra cùng một sự thay đổi pH.

segments.src: This is exactly why soil test reports include a buffer pH.*
segments.tr: Đây chính là lý do tại sao các báo cáo xét nghiệm đất bao gồm pH đệm.*

segments.src: ***Q3 → B.** Iron becomes progressively less soluble as pH rises; in alkaline soil it precipitates into forms roots cannot absorb.
segments.tr: ***Q3 → B.** Sắt trở nên ít hòa tan hơn khi độ pH tăng; trong đất kiềm, nó kết tủa thành các dạng mà rễ không thể hấp thụ.

segments.src: The plant is iron-deficient despite iron being physically present — a good illustration that total nutrient content and plant-available nutrient content are two different things.
segments.tr: Cây bị thiếu sắt mặc dù sắt vẫn hiện diện vật lý — một minh chứng rõ ràng rằng tổng hàm lượng dinh dưỡng và hàm lượng dinh dưỡng cây có thể hấp thụ là hai điều khác nhau.

segments.src: Interveinal chlorosis on the youngest leaves is the classic symptom, because iron is not readily remobilized within the plant.*
segments.tr: Bệnh úa vàng giữa các gân lá trên những lá non nhất là triệu chứng điển hình, vì sắt không dễ dàng được huy động lại trong cây.*
